💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United have been offered an intriguing opportunity to bring Scott McTominay back to Old Trafford as uncertainty grows over his future at Napoli.
  • The Scotland international has transformed his reputation since leaving United in 2024, becoming a key figure in Naples and helping the club win Serie A.
  • However, with his contract moving towards its final 18 months and renewal talks making little progress, a Premier League return in 2027 is now becoming increasingly realistic.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have been offered an intriguing opportunity to bring Scott McTominay back to Old Trafford as uncertainty grows over his future at Napoli.

The Scotland international has transformed his reputation since leaving United in 2024, becoming a key figure in Naples and helping the club win Serie A.

However, with his contract moving towards its final 18 months and renewal talks making little progress, a Premier League return in 2027 is now becoming increasingly realistic.

According to TEAMtalk, intermediaries are exploring potential destinations for McTominay in case Napoli fail to reach an agreement over a newly introduced contract.

Man United have been informed of the situation and have not dismissed the possibility of re-signing their former academy graduate.

Industry observers note that mcTominay remains open to staying in Naples, but discussions over an extension have stalled. Chelsea, AC Milan and Juventus are also monitoring developments, while clubs from Saudi Arabia have shown interest.

A return to Old Trafford would be particularly interesting following Mauricio Pochettino’s appointment, with United expected to reshape their midfield in 2027.

United sold McTominay at a point when he was often viewed as a useful squad player rather than a guaranteed starter.

It has been revealed that that perception has changed dramatically. A recent CaughtOffside report highlighted how his performances in Italy have turned him into a much more complete midfielder, capable of contributing both defensively and in the final third.

Industry observers note that that profile could appeal to Pochettino. McTominay already understands the club, the league and the pressure surrounding United, meaning there would be virtually no adaptation period. His goalscoring ability from midfield could also become particularly valuable if Bruno Fernandes eventually leaves.

The obvious concern is price. United would effectively be paying to re-sign a player they sold for far less only a few years earlier, which would inevitably invite criticism.

But recruitment decisions should be judged on the player United would be buying now, not the one they sold in 2024.

In a recent development, if Napoli’s contract talks continue to stall and the fee becomes reasonable, a McTominay return should be taken seriously. He left Old Trafford as a useful midfielder, he could return as a considerably better one.

Juventus look to Nick Woltemade and Randal Kolo Muani in attack as they host struggling Venezia in a must-win game at the Allianz Stadium.

The Bianconeri are still dealing with an injury crisis, but Andrea Cambiaso and Zeki Celik are available, and the Turkishman is competing with Federico Gatti for a starting spot in a back three, as Sky and Gazzetta report.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Celtic's 4-1 dispatching of St Mirren on Saturday afternoon suggests Martin O'Neill might have got his side back on track, with one of his veteran operators showing just how key he could be for the remainder of the campaign.

The Hoops started the month badly with defeat at Falkirk and only edged out bottom side Kilmarnock by a single goal heading into the international break, so it was a welcome return to something the dominance expected of the Scottish Premiership leaders this weekend.

While they had plenty of possession and opportunities early on it took until 33 minutes in for Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain to open the scoring after a pair of Camilo Duran efforts were ruled out for infringements.

The Colombian quickly added a second, and Luke McCowan a third before the break as the home side took complete control, with Callum McGregor's fourth just after the hour putting the game to bed despite a late consolation penalty from Killian Phillips.

The attacking trio of Duran, flanked on either side by Jota and Yang Hyun-Jun, may have been the most eye-catching on the day, but there is a strong argument to say that it was Oxlade-Chamberlain who really shone through in victory.

It was the veteran Englishman's first goal of the campaign and a crucial intervention as the breakthrough opened the floodgates and allowed Celtic to have the game mostly wrapped up by half-time.

The Champions League winner has been in and out of O'Neill's lineup so far this season as the side have lurched through various periods of inconsistency, despite still leading the title race.

Oxlade-Chamberlain had been largely ever-present in O'Neill's second stint in charge last term, arriving in January after leaving Besiktas as a free agent, but disappeared to the bench for the post-split run-in as the Hoops surged back to pip Hearts to the title on the final day.

The ex-England international surely will have staked a hefty claim for a few more starts after his strong showing in central midfield, which saw him rated 8/10 by 67 Hail Hail after the final whistle.

Oxlade-Chamberlain vs St Mirren.

Even if he can only last an hour or so like he did here the veteran proved he can make a difference in the early running before making way for a closer to see things out.

The Scottish Premiership often demonstrates late-career stars that it is no walk in the park but the former Liverpool and Arsenal man was able to show plenty of the quality on the ball that made him a Premier League regular, fitness permitting, earlier in his career.

According to stats compiled by FootMob Oxlade-Chamberlain had 43 attacking touches in his 61 minutes on the pitch, but his passing was close to flawless.

As well as his goal he was accurate with 29 of his 32 passes, including all three of his long balls, and was only dispossessed twice in the game while making five passes into the final third.

He may not have the legs he once had as a winger at Southampton and Arsenal but the vision and the touch that characterised the middle of his career was on full display.

At his best it shouldn't be too controversial to suggest that Oxlade-Chamberlain can be O'Neill's best player, and could be crucial in steadying a side that has been swaying all too often this term.

His well-documented injury issues and advancing years will of course mean his best is unlikely to be on show week in and week out, but if the manager and his staff can keep the midfielder match fit and able to get somewhere close to his best he can be a key asset for the rest of the campaign.

Play was brought to a standstill during Austriaâs 2026 World Cup qualifier against Cyprus after a sinkhole suddenly appeared on the pitch late in the second half.

The bizarre incident occurred around the 75th minute, when Danish referee Jakob Kehlet halted the match after noticing the gaping hole near Austria keeper Alexander Schlagerâs box at the Raiffeisen Arena, in Linz.

The opening was wide enough to swallow an entire football, prompting ground staff to rush on with buckets of sand in a frantic attempt to patch it up.

After more than seven minutes of repairs, Kehlet finally gave the green light to resume, with Austria eventually sealing a 1-0 win thanks to Marcel Sabitzerâs second-half penalty â scored before the ground gave way.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino is gearing up for his first match in charge of Manchester United on Sunday, but work will already be underway behind the scenes on strengthening his squad in the January transfer window.

Man United travel to Anfield on Sunday to face Liverpool lying 19th in the Premier League table, which highlights just how bad their beginning to the campaign has been.

A point would be enough to lift the Red Devils out of the bottom three, and that will be the minimum aim for Pochettino as he looks to make a positive start to life as United manager.

The 54-year-old will have to do that without two of the club's best attackers, with their first-choice striker Benjamin Sesko likely to be out until 2027.

GIVEMESPORT also revealed on Saturday evening that Marcus Rashford will miss the trip to Merseyside, despite hope that he, Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw would be available for selection for the former Spurs boss.

Reports have suggested that Pochettino has 'always loved' Rashford, having tried to sign him for Tottenham previously, and it will be interesting to see if they can strike up a successful partnership together when he returns.

The absence of Rashford means that, unless he chooses to start Shea Lacey, the front four is likely to be Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes, Bryan Mbeumo and Amad Diallo at Anfield.

Mbeumo and Cunha have largely shared the centre-forward role in Sesko's absence this term, but neither has been convincing in the role, and it is no surprise that GMS understands a new striker is a priority in the January window.

According to the Telegraph, their US sources claim that Pochettino could ask the club to sign Monaco striker Folarin Balogun, who has been in fine form under the Argentine at international level.

GMS sources understand that Balogun would be 'very open' to making a move to the Premier League in 2027, having come close to joining Everton in the summer after they agreed a £40m deal with Monaco.

A separate report has claimed that the 25-year-old would be ready to listen to an offer from United after Pochettino was confirmed as Michael Carrick's successor, such is the strength of his relationship with the 54-year-old.

If Pochettino wants him, and he is keen to make the switch to Old Trafford, then it increases the likelihood of a January transfer, as long as a suitable deal can be agreed between the Red Devils and Monaco.

It would be a big outlay for United to pay £40m for him mid-season, and perhaps a loan deal with an option or obligation to buy would be a better option for them, if the Ligue 1 giants would give the green light to that.

Balogun, described as being 'insane' by international teammate Christian Pulisic, could be exactly what United need too, given their struggles when the likes of Mbeumo and Cunha have played as a 9 this season.

The former Arsenal forward has scored goals wherever he has been, from Stade Reims to Monaco, and for the United States, and if the likes of Bruno Fernandes are feeding him, you would expect him to score goals in a red shirt.

GMS sources revealed previously that the Red Devils have an interest in Dominic Calvert-Lewin at Leeds United, although the England international is expected to sign a new contract at Elland Road.

Elsewhere, there have been links to Victor Osimhen of Galatasaray, but that is another move that appears unlikely given his salary and how much it would cost to prise him away from the Turkish giants.

Balogun could be their most realistic option in the winter market, and it will be interesting to see if he is the striker the club and Pochettino decide to make a move on.

According to TEAMtalk, Man United, Liverpool and Chelsea are all monitoring Scalvini, with clubs carrying out detailed checks as they assess potential centre-back signings.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Success in football comes in circles, as good times come and go for every club, but some clubs have far more consistent cycles than others.

Many clubs have had generations of success through each era of football, through multiple competitions, managers, rule changes and players, as the cream always rises to the top.

The 2026-27 campaign got underway in August, but most of the trophies won't be dished out until the second half of the campaign.

According to recent reports, as we deep dive into the stories of these footballing superpowers, it's essential to understand that every title, every cup, every league win has a backdrop. Stories of grit, magic moments, unforgettable comebacks, and yes, heartbreaks too. Every piece of silverware is a chapter in the illustrious book of their history.

Sources indicate that prepare for an exhilarating journey. A trip through football's hall of fame, where tales of dramatic finals, footballing dynasties, and players who've become larger than life await.

While trophies do stand testament to a club's success, it's the culture, the traditions, and the die-hard fans that truly capture its essence. As we profile these titans, we're not just tallying their victories but celebrating the undying spirit that's made them legendary. Because remember, in football, the journey is just as important, if not more, than the destination. Let the games begin.

According to recent reports, bulgarian powerhouse CSKA Sofia are first up on our list and are probably not the first club you would think of when it comes to success in football. Nevertheless, they have won an astonishing 57 trophies in their history - a legacy that few can rival in Eastern European circles.

Established in 1948, they have maintained a firm grip on domestic football in their nation, which has undoubtedly impressed fans and foes alike. Their fierce rivalries and iconic moments against the likes of Levski Sofia have left an indelible mark on the football world, known as "The Eternal Derby of Bulgaria.".

Zamalek are certainly not a football team that rolls across the tongue as easily as some of the top sides in Europe do, but this team has, over the years, boasted an iron grip on domestic football in Egypt and have dominated the scene since the club was established in 1911.

According to recent reports, they are not only a cornerstone of Egyptian football, but also for Africa as a whole. Their 58-trophy haul has been a testament to their resilience and consistency. The iconic Cairo derby between them and Al Ahly is a spectacle, a footballing carnival that never ceases to amaze. It has been branded in the past as "the world's most violent derby" - though, remarkably, Zamalek aren't the only Egyptian side on this list.

According to recent reports, founded in 1970, PSG are among the youngest clubs on this list. But after winning four trophies in the 2024/25 campaign - including their first-ever Champions League triumph - and then doing the same again just a season on, they have undoubtedly earned their place among the most prestigious and decorated clubs in the world.

It has been revealed that luis Enrique is building something truly magnificent in Paris, and Les Parisiens are certainly here to stay, boasting a young squad that includes the likes of Joao Neves, Desire Doue, Vitinha, and many others. Furthermore, having won 13 of the last 15 Ligue 1 seasons with relative ease, continued domestic dominance seems almost guaranteed.

In a recent development, FCSB might not mean a lot to some, but if you say Steaua Bucharest, then things start to make a lot more sense. FCSB's 62 trophies firmly entrench them as Romania's best club by far. The club isn't even 100 years old yet but has achieved more in Europe than other clubs in neighbouring countries could ever dream of. Steaua's European Cup win in 1986, otherwise known as the 'Miracle of 86,' is something that the club is incredibly proud of, and rightly so.

They went on to produce one of the longest unbeaten streaks that's ever been seen for the next three years. This club is the shining example of a true underdog. Even though they are the best team in their country by quite some distance, they are still considered minnows to the rest of Europe. That being said, with a European Cup to their name, their supporters would argue otherwise.

Recent findings suggest that boca Juniors are one of the most famous clubs in the world and arguably have a global reach that matches or exceeds some of the top sides in Europe. Their famous blue and yellow strips are synonymous throughout the world of football, especially for the performances of Diego Maradona - easily one of the greatest players of all time - though it has been a while since someone with that presence made an impact on the team.

The Argentine club secured their 62nd and most-recent trophy in November 2026, defeating Brazilian side Atletico-MG in the final of the CONMEBOL Sudamericana - South America's equivalent of the UEFA Europa League.

Galatasaray stand tall and proud as a symbol of Turkish footballing might. The cauldron of noise that is generated at their Turk Telekom Arena makes it a venue most European adversaries dread, a tale that has lived since the early 1990s when Manchester United visited for the first time - alongside a famous Tifo that stated: "Welcome to Hell.".

But it's not only the Red Devils who have felt the wrath of the brilliant football club over the years. Because of the help from their passionate supporters, and the valiant efforts on the pitch in the club's famous red and yellow colours, they have clinched no more but no less than 64 trophies, their latest being yet another league and cup double, and they will continue to etch unforgettable memories into the history of Galatasaray.

Next up are the Belgian giants Anderlecht, who have remained competitive for as long as many of us can remember. It seemed like every year that they would face Manchester United in the Champions League, and there's a good reason for that: their unrelenting success on the domestic stage.

With 64 trophies to their name since their founding in 1908, this showcases how consistent they have been over the years in the Belgian Pro League and other cup competitions they are able to participate in. When football fans think of purple and white colours, the first club that comes to their head is Anderlecht.

Croatian giants Dinamo Zagreb are next up on the list, as one of the most well-known names in eastern European football. Their domination of Croatian football has seen them as regulars on the continental stage, although their European success has been sparse in recent years.

With 68 trophies, Dinamo are tied for major honours with arguably the biggest club in the world, Manchester United, and are the only Croatian club to have won a continental trophy, albeit when the nation was part of Yugoslavia, having won the 1966-67 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup, beating Don Revie's Leeds United in the final, having beaten Juventus along the way.

If you say the 'Theatre of Dreams', Old Trafford, or the 'Busby Babes' to someone, there's only one club that comes to mind: Manchester United. Their 68 trophies paint a tale of legends, right from the 'Busby Babes' Munich air disaster in 1958 to the 'Class of 92'. Icons like the late Sir Bobby Charlton, who passed in 2023, Eric Cantona and Wayne Rooney, to name a few, have donned the famous red jersey.

Sources indicate that while the club has struggled to hit the heights of the 1990s and 2000s since Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement in 2013, they remain level as the most successful club in England - and with three Champions Leagues to their name, one of the best teams to have ever played in Europe, as well. The question is: how much longer will it be before United are fighting for football's biggest trophies again?

A club that needs no introduction. Liverpool Football Club is a footballing household name around the world. Anfield roars with the Reds' anthem of "You'll Never Walk Alone". Adopted courtesy of Gerry and the Pacemakers back in the 1960s, it's a song that transcends boundaries and unites football lovers across the globe.

With 68 trophies, Liverpool's legacy speaks of European nights, iconic comebacks, and legendary figures like Bill Shankly and Kenny Dalglish. Having won their first league title in 30 years in 2020, they only had to wait another five to get their hands on it again, with Arne Slot's debut campaign sending the Reds back to the top of the Premier League thanks to the heroics of stars like Mohamed Salah and Virgil van Dijk.

Milan will look to Gonçalo Ramos, Christian Pulisic and Adrien Rabiot in a tricky Serie A game against Serie A surprise Frosinone.

It kicks off at 18:00 CET [17:00 GMT] at San Siro.

Samuel Chukwueze, Fikayo Tomori, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Matteo Gabbia and Alexis Saelemaekers are injured for the home side, while Strahinja Pavlović is available but not fit to start, according to Sky and Gazzetta.

Therefore, Sankhoun Diawara is expected to join Koni De Winter at centre-back, with Davide Bartesaghi at left-back and Mario Gila at right-back.

Pulisic has returned from international duty after scoring a banger against Haiti on Tuesday and will start alongside Rabiot behind sole striker Ramos.

Industry observers note that frosinone are without their best scorer, Antonio Raimondo, who is still injured. Left-back Gabriele Bracaglia is another notable absentee as the Italian left-back serves a one-game ban.

It has been revealed that the match will be broadcast live on DAZN in the UK and Ireland and on Paramount+ in the USA. Football Italia will provide live updates via a live blog for all five Serie A matches today, including Juventus-Venezia.

Milan (4-4-1-1): Maignan, Gila, De Winter, Diawara, Bartesaghi, Moreira, Musah, Modric, Pulisic, Rabiot, Matias Ramos.

Frosinone (4-2-3-1): Palmisani, Oyono, Calvani, Monterisi, Tchato, Masini, Calò, Ghedjemis, Schmid, Kvernadze, Bîrligea.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Around the world, people are demanding a halt to the proliferation of data centres — racks of computers, housed in warehouses, that are powering the boom in artificial intelligence.
  • Recent findings suggest that is the climate totally cooked?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that AI companies must engage with those who oppose the expansion of data centres.Credit: Michael M. Santiago/Getty.

Around the world, people are demanding a halt to the proliferation of data centres — racks of computers, housed in warehouses, that are powering the boom in artificial intelligence. Communities worry that existing infrastructure will not be able to handle the surge in demand for electricity and water, and that data centres’ energy demands will cause environmental and health problems, including increases in air pollution and greenhouse-gas emissions. The question of whether AI is going to stall climate action is explored in the first of a three-part Nature Podcast (Nature https://doi.org/rzqs; 2026).

Is the climate totally cooked? What the data say.

Recent findings suggest that is the climate totally cooked? What the data say.

Industry observers note that people have many concerns about the way AI is being developed, including how it might affect safety, security and jobs. Where energy is concerned, however, any added demand for computing power can, and must, be met in smart, sustainable ways, not by burning more fossil fuels. Achieving this will take some creative thinking, and researchers need to be closely involved. Many argue that there are alternatives to relying on energy-intensive data centres, such as AI models that can run on individual computers or institutional servers, thereby consuming much less power than those run using cloud services. Efforts to develop such options need to be better funded.

In a recent development, future projections of data centres’ energy demands are hard to make, because they are based on assumptions that could change. If current global trends continue, electricity consumption by data centres will go on rising. Between 2017 and 2024, it grew by around 12% per year. Figures for 2024 from the International Energy Agency (IEA), based in Paris, show most of this demand coming from three regions: the United States (45%), China (25%) and Europe (15%).

Sources indicate that the Electric Power Research Institute, a non-profit organization in Palo Alto, California, has projected that the continued growth of US data centres could add up to 94 gigawatts of demand by 2030, equivalent to 17% of the country’s electricity consumption. Data centres presently consume more than 1.5% of the world’s electricity supply, and the IEA’s projections indicate that this figure will more than double in the next few years. By 2030, data centres could consume more electricity than Japan, the agency notes.

Why scientists should lead the shift away from AI mega data centres.

Why scientists should lead the shift away from AI mega data centres.

In a recent development, there are serious concerns that this extra demand will be powered mainly by fossil fuels, when carbon emissions are already at a record high. Research published this week in Nature Sustainability estimates that some 400 data centres in the United States accounted for around 26 megatonnes of carbon dioxide emissions between May 2024 and April 2025, more than those produced by many countries (G. Guidi et al. Nature Sustain. https://doi.org/hcsptc; 2026). And according to a study published last week in Nature Climate Change, data centres’ energy demands could prolong the lifespan of coal-fired power stations (C. Li et al. Nature Clim. Change https://doi.org/rzqr; 2026).

It has been revealed that but none of this is inevitable. Governments could mandate that new energy demand be met with renewable sources. And regulators could look at alternative ways to manage existing electric supplies.

Many nations’ electric grid systems are designed to accommodate surges in demand, whether to power extra cooling on hot summer days or extra heating during winter cold snaps. Much of the time, there is excess capacity. This excess could be used to reduce the amount of latest energy needed to power data centres.

How much energy will AI really consume? The good, the bad and the unknown.

Recent findings suggest that how much energy will AI really consume? The good, the bad and the unknown.

According to recent reports, one solution is to curtail data-centre operations during periods of peak electricity consumption, and ramp up at times of lower demand. An analysis released in 2025 by researchers at Duke University in Durham, North Carolina, found that the US electric grid could accommodate 98 gigawatts of extra demand in this way, without adding any new generation capacity (see go.nature.com/4cdeknm). That 98 gigawatts would be enough to cover most, if not all, of the expected expansion in US data centres over the next few years.

It has been revealed that there is potential for this to become a reality. In June, as part of a larger effort to modernize the grid, the US Federal Energy Regulatory Commission instructed grid operators to draw up a proposal for how they will cope with extra demand from data centres. The technology industry is understandably paying close attention to how it might mitigate the problems of powering data centres. Earlier this month, OpenAI announced what it is calling a “grid protectors program”, a project to consult with US grid operators, regulators and policymakers to see how the company can work around peaks in power demand.

It has been revealed that meanwhile, Google is paying households and businesses in parts of the Eastern United States to reduce their electricity consumption during periods of high demand. Similar proposals are being considered in other countries.

Why open-source generative AI models are an ethical way forward for science.

Why open-source generative AI models are an ethical way forward for science.

These are all tentative moves in the right direction, although arguably progress is not being made fast enough. Policymakers and data-centre operators must engage seriously with those who oppose the centres’ expansion. At a minimum, any new energy sources developed to power these centres must be renewable. Existing energy sources can also be better deployed, and researchers working to develop alternatives to energy-intensive data centres should be better supported. More peer-reviewed evidence is needed, especially for countries outside the United States.

Sources indicate that there are smarter and more sustainable ways to power the growth of AI, but to achieve them, concerted and coordinated action will be needed. In this way, the harm posed to people and the planet can be minimized, and AI technologies can benefit everyone.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 04:25 EST, 22 November 2026.

When Mauricio Pochettino boarded a flight from London to Atlanta a little over two weeks ago, there was little indication that by the time he landed back in the UK it would be as the fresh head coach of Manchester United.

The club were aware of the £7.5million buyout clause in his contract with the US national team as they began to consider potential replacements for Michael Carrick, but it hadn’t gone any further than that.

Recent findings suggest that however, United’s 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth on October 25 left Carrick’s job hanging by a thread. He was given a two-week stay of execution that also allowed United time to step up their search for a suitable replacement.

At a meeting of the club’s executive committee on November 5 – after United had lost to Chelsea and staged a chaotic Champions League win against Roma – it was decided that Pochettino would be the No.1 choice if Carrick was sacked.

By the time the Argentine caught that flight to Atlanta 24 hours later to take charge of the USA's two-legged CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final against Haiti, United were preparing to make their move.

This is the story of the whirlwind two weeks that will end with Pochettino taking charge of his first game as United boss against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday following the dramatic events on both sides of the Atlantic.

Industry observers note that patrick Dorgu’s injury-time header rescued United from another defeat as they snatched a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa at Old Trafford, but it wasn’t enough to save Carrick. His fate was effectively sealed and the first contact was made with Pochettino’s camp.

There is a five-hour time difference between Manchester and Georgia, so it was late afternoon when Pochettino first learned of United’s interest at the Trilith Guesthouse – close to the US national team’s training base in Fayetteville south-west of Atlanta – as the players began to report there for duty.

Michael Carrick's fate was effectively sealed and the first contact was made with Pochettino’s camp after the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford.

As speculation raged over Carrick’s future, the odds on Pochettino replacing him at Old Trafford were slashed after some significant money was placed on the 54-year-old overnight.

Preliminary talks continued with his representatives who made the US Soccer Federation aware of the situation. Pochettino discussed it over dinner at the team hotel with chief executive JT Batson and chief operating officer Dan Helfrich who knew it was pointless trying to change his mind.

‘That was the major day,’ indicates a source close to Pochettino, who took US team training in Fayetteville. ‘It became real and the optimism grew.’.

As talks accelerated between United and their prospective upcoming head coach, Carrick returned to Carrington to work with the United players not on international duty while chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox flew to Monaco to meet minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and rubber-stamp the change.

United reached verbal agreement with Pochettino over a two-and-a-half-year deal, and agreed to pay US Soccer around £10million to buy the 54-year-old and his staff – No 2 Jesus Perez, first-team coach Miguel D’Agostino, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez, fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino (Mauricio’s son), strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya and analyst Alec Scott – out of their contracts.

There was never any question of him leaving before the two Haiti ties, even though it left little time before his first game against Liverpool. Pochettino is remarked to have been respectful of the USA’s position and felt an obligation to see the job through.

As a compromise, it was agreed that Perez, Jimenez and Pochettino Jnr would be allowed to leave for Manchester after the first leg regardless of the result.

Media in the US were informed that access to the players had been cancelled out of respect for Veterans Day. It also meant that they don’t have to answer questions about Pochettino’s future.

Carrick returned to Carrington at 7.50am for the last time as United head coach and was sacked in a meeting with Berrada and Wilcox.

By the time Pochettino woke up in Fayetteville, United officially had a managerial vacancy and he gathered the players together for a scheduled team briefing at 10am.

Pochettino went through the usual pre-match preparation, and then invited staff into the room for the second half of the meeting.

There was some emotion but no surprise when he informed them of his decision to take the United job. ‘As you’d expect, he spoke from the heart,’ notes a source. ‘He loved being here but United was a dream opportunity. It was too hard to say no, but hard to say goodbye.’.

United officially declared Pochettino’s appointment and confirmed that he would stay in charge for the USA’s two games against Haiti before starting work the following Wednesday.

Pochettino conducted his pre-match press conference in Fayetteville, flanked by CEO chief JT Batson and president Cindy Parlow Cone, and broke down in tears as he thanked them for their support over the last 26 months.

Otherwise, the preparation is said to have gone according to blueprint as the US squad flew to Miami.

The Argentine broke down in tears as he thanked the USA for their support over the last 26 months.

The US smashed Haiti 6-0 to all but guarantee their place in the semi-finals. Even so the message from Pochettino to his players after the game was: ‘This tie isn’t over.’.

The players learned for the first time that Perez, Jimenez and Pochettino Jnr were leaving camp, and they headed straight to Manchester.

Pochettino flew with the players from Miami to Cincinnati for the second leg at the TQL Stadium.

On a visit to the Kenwood Towne Centre shopping mall, a man whose profile had risen in the US during his two years in charge of the national team was approached by even more fans than normal.

When Pochettino appeared as a guest of honour at the NFL game between the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium that night, a number of Bengals’ players and staff congratulated him on his upcoming job claiming to be United fans.

It emerged that United had provided a private jet for Pochettino and the remainder of his staff to fly straight from Cincinnati to Manchester through the night after the second leg.

In his pre-match press conference, he confirmed the departure of his three coaches over the weekend, and it was no surprise to learn that he was in constant contact over several days as he prepared to join them at Carrington.

It has been revealed that the US beat Haiti by two goals to complete an 8-0 aggregate win. Afterwards, they played Take Me Home, Country Roads by John Denver over the stadium PA, which has been a tradition since the US hosted the World Cup last summer but carried particular poignance given that it has also been adopted as an anthem at United.

Pochettino invited all the staff onto the pitch for a team photo as he led a chant of U-S-A, and there was a tearful send-off in the dressing-room as he was presented with a signed shirt and a special hand-painted bottle of Clase Azul tequila.

It’s a favourite tipple of Pochettino’s and staff also ordered food from Chick-fil-A, which Pochettino regrets won’t be available in Manchester.

He never had a permanent residence in America, so he left the stadium at 10.30pm with the same suitcase he had brought from London and headed for Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport for the flight to Manchester.

Pochettino had a poor night’s sleep before landing shortly before noon aboard the grey Gulfstream G700 jet with D’Agostino, Scott and Tuya.

He posted a picture from the skies above Manchester and was then driven to Carrington, changing into an official United tracksuit en route.

Pochettino was too late for training but met with some of the players and club executives before being given a tour of the training ground and conducting an interview with MUTV which wrapped up about 7pm. He stayed at the training ground long into the evening to catch up on his preparation for Liverpool.

The plane believed to be carrying Pochettino and his staff was hired by Manchester United.

Recent findings suggest that more players returned from international duty, but Pochettino’s first training session with them at Carrington was ambushed by a drone shooting video footage that was posted online. It was proof – if he needed it – that the former Tottenham and Chelsea boss will be under even greater scrutiny at United.

Responding, Pochettino said: 'We have young guys training with us. It’s not nice. It’s not good.

'What do they want to show? Yes, we were working on shape. We were very organised. What is the point of doing something that can be very dangerous?

'I don't want to be upset, but I think it's a process the club is caring a lot about.'.

Pochettino’s first training session with them at Carrington was ambushed by a drone shooting video footage that was posted online.

Having only trained for a couple of hours on Thursday, Pochettino worked with the players between 11.30am and 2pm on Friday.

‘The training session was a little bit longer than it normally is in (match day) minus two,’ stated Pochettino at his opening pre-match press conference, admitting that he had not even had a chance to shower beforehand.

Pochettino worked with his new players between 11.30am and 2pm on Friday.

Pochettino took training for the third day running at Carrington on Saturday morning, before United travelled on the team bus to their hotel where they had dinner and a pre-match meeting last night.

On Sunday he faces a massive first game as United boss in front of the cameras at Anfield at the end of a dizzying fortnight.

Breaking: Germany's 2027 budget: A record €561 billion and a mountain of debt

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that it was 5:55 a.m.
  • Sources indicate that following nearly 16 hours of negotiations, lawmakers from the conservative Christian Democratic Union(CDU) and Christian Social Union (CSU) parties, along with their coalition partners from the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD), voted in favor of the 2027 draft budget.
  • Reading through the nearly 1,000-page document requires a great deal of number-crunching.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that it was 5:55 a.m. on Friday when the Bundestag's Budget Committee concluded its final session.

Sources indicate that following nearly 16 hours of negotiations, lawmakers from the conservative Christian Democratic Union(CDU) and Christian Social Union (CSU) parties, along with their coalition partners from the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD), voted in favor of the 2027 draft budget. The opposition parties — the environmentalist Greens, the socialist Left Party and the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) — voted against it. With that, the way is now clear for the final vote in the Bundestag on November 27.

Reading through the nearly 1,000-page document requires a great deal of number-crunching. Next year, the federal government plans to spend around €561 billion ($620 billion).

But here's the problem: it won't collect nearly enough revenue to cover these expenses. With a shortfall of €123 billion, borrowing will be needed to bridge the gap.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

But that's not the only problem. On top of all this debt, Germany also has loans for defense spending and for the renovation of the dilapidated infrastructure. Approved by the Bundestag in 2025, these special funds are set to be in place for multiple years.

According to recent reports, if the new debt for 2027 is factored in, the total borrowing amounts to over €210 billion. This is the second-highest level of borrowing in the history of the Federal Republic of Germany. The only time Germany borrowed more was during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2021, when borrowing reached €215.4 billion.

Industry observers note that this development has drawn sharp criticism from opposition parties. Green Party lawmaker Sebastian Schäfer and his colleague Dietmar Bartsch of the Left Party called it a "gigantic mountain of debt," an "untrustworthy" budget, "irresponsible" policies at the expense of future generations and a lack of future prospects.

In a recent development, to understand the reasons behind the growing debt, one has to look beyond the numbers. Every federal budget is a snapshot of the priorities set by a government and a country — in terms of the economy, social issues, security and geopolitics.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that for 2027, that story continues to be one of crises and wars. While Russia's war against Ukraine is driving up defense spending, the faltering economy is also demanding new investments. At the same time, Germany's population is aging rapidly, which is driving up social spending.

In a recent development, what's more, the crumbling infrastructure must be repaired and modernized, and the energy transition is costing billions. And more than half of all this debt is going toward security and defense.

In a recent development, russia's war against Ukraine will enter its sixth year in 2027. As of the end of June, the federal government estimated its overall support for Ukraine to have reached approximately €100 billion. In response to a request from the AfD in the Bundestag, the government stated: "The federal government will continue to provide Ukraine with political, financial, humanitarian, civil and military support for as long as necessary.".

The rearmament of the Bundeswehr and spending on NATO are also putting massive pressure on the budget. The defense budget is set to grow to just under €110 billion in 2027, an increase of around €27 billion compared to last year. Added to this are expenditures from the Bundeswehr's special fund.

In a recent development, nevertheless, by far the largest single budget item comes from the Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs, which is set to grow to over €200 billion. There are plans for cost-cutting measures, for example, in basic income support for job seekers. But the costs of old-age pension benefits continue to rise.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, people born in the 1960s have begun to retire. Back then, more than 1 million children were born each year. But birth rates nearly halved in the early 1970s and have continued to decline since then. As a result, there will be an increasing number of retirees and a decreasing number of working-age individuals in the coming years.

Recent findings suggest that the pension funds cannot be financed by the pension contributions of this dwindling workforce and have to be subsidized by the government. Already, contributions to the pension insurance system — which are split equally between employees and employers — will have to be increased. They are expected to rise to just under 20% of gross salary.

Recent findings suggest that the Federal Employment Agency, too, has long been unable to make ends meet on contributions alone. In 2027, subsidies of more than €8 billion from the federal budget are planned.

In a recent development, anyone comparing Germany's current budget situation with that of past years will be rubbing their eyes in disbelief. It wasn't that long ago that Germany was considered a model of fiscal discipline. Between 2014 and 2019, the federal budget managed to avoid taking on latest debt for six consecutive years. In some years, there was even money left over.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

But the era of "balanced budgets" came to an abrupt end with the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020. However, today Germany is still enjoying the benefits of those years of fiscal stability. Compared to other countries, Germany is still in relatively good shape.

It has been revealed that the key indicator is not the amount of debt along but the debt-to-GDP ratio. It indicates how high the national debt is in relation to annual economic output.

In a recent development, at the end of 2025, it stood at 63.5% for Germany. France, on the other hand, stands at over 110% and Italy at about 135% to 140%, while the US is well above 100%. However, in its latest fall report, the German Council of Economic Experts warned that Germany could be heading down a dangerous path. If debt continues to rise at this rate, the debt-to-GDP ratio could climb to 100% by 2040.

It has been revealed that this would also put Germany's creditworthiness on the financial markets at risk. Germany is the only country among the seven leading democratic industrialized nations (G7) that still holds a triple-A (AAA) rating. This is the highest possible credit rating on the financial markets. It signals to investors that the risk of default on German government bonds is extremely low.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that this also means that interest rates on new loans are not set as high. This is an important point, as interest payments place an increasing burden on the federal budget each year. By 2027, approximately €42 billion in interest payments are expected to be due.

At the end of November, the Bundestag will hold its final debate on the draft budget. Should changes be expected by then? There is disagreement within the government over whether a reduction in the electricity tax might still be possible.

The prospect of such a reduction had been raised by Chancellor Friedrich Merz. On Friday, during a European leaders summit in Dublin, he reiterated: "I expect that we will discuss this again next Tuesday in the coalition committee, and I remain committed to my goal of lowering the electricity tax to the European minimum — in full — starting next year.".

At full-time, Chelsea players went to applaud those fans who had stayed until the end, but Palmer could be spotted seething as he made a bee-line to the tunnel.

His decision to avoid clapping the home support prompted coach Willie Isa and injured teammate Joao Pedro to intervene and try to change his mind. Careful to mask his words with his hand, Palmer strutted up to teammate Pedro with a raised eyebrow, continuing to look angry as he refused to reconsider. Watch the incident below:.

This weekend's result was made even more damaging by the fact Moises Caicedo had to be taken off through injury in the first-half. The Blues may find some solace in the form of back-to-back fixtures against relegation candidates Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace, but they then face the daunting task of turning their form around against Liverpool and Manchester City.

Alonso - who now finds himself under growing pressure in the Stamford Bridge hot seat - was asked about Palmer's full-time actions, to which he responded to the media (watch below):.

“We were disappointed, the fans were disappointed. We understand their frustration because expectations are high, and we feel sorry for them. We are in a fragile moment, but we need to work together and stick together. There is still a long way to go.”.

It would seem the Spaniard was eager to stay away from the controversy, having been more concerned about trying to turn his side's form around.

Newcastle United hosted Arsenal in the Premier League on Saturday evening, and fans were not happy about the state of the team even before a ball was kicked.

The Magpies started with a team that looked very weak on paper, including young midfielders Seun Steur and Lewis Miley playing, with Joe Willock in midfield, and Jacob Murphy in attack alongside William Osula and Harvey Barnes.

The substitutes' bench saw much stronger options available, including the likes of Matias Fernandez-Pardo, Anthony Elanga, Nico Gonzalez, Yoanne Wissa, Tino Livramento, Jacob Ramsey, and Sven Botman.

But perhaps more significantly was the fact that two summer signings in Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Toure were not included in the matchday squad at all by Matthias Jaissle, despite the club spending £72m on the pair under Eddie Howe.

Neither player was expected to be ready to make an immediate impact on the starting lineup this season considering their age, profile, and experience at the top level. But to not be included in the squad at all, despite the clear challenges that the squad is having this season, suggests that the manager has no faith in their qualities.

It's also worth noting that Newcastle were without Joelinton for the game, with the Brazilian injured and unavailable for selection. That would imply that both players are even further down the pecking order than it may seem initially.

In a recent development, bamba's lack of involvement is potentially not as worrying, because of the options in midfield. Steur has been pushing for an opportunity, and with Nico Gonzalez on the bench, and Jaissle a huge fan of Willock, him being left out on this occasion can be excused.

But for Toure, the situation is hugely different. Newcastle have been struggling for goals all season, managing just 13 goals in their 10 games before the Arsenal fixture, and their top scorers Barnes, Willock, and Elanga all have just two goals each.

It has been revealed that other attacking options in the squad have struggled to make any sort of impact too, while Toure has two goals this season despite having started just one game in all competitions. His incredible pace, dribbling ability, and creativity should mean that he should at least be considered by a manager looking for ways to turn the team's fortunes around.

When Newcastle agreed a £42m deal to sign Toure from Hoffenheim, it was with the idea of him becoming an integral part of the future of the club under Eddie Howe.

But before the season even began Howe had left, and it now looks evident that Toure is not someone that Jaissle wants as part of his squad.

The Ivorian hasn't started a game since August, and despite the team winning just three of their opening ten games in the Premier League, he can't get a look in. Jaissle has no interest in giving Toure an opportunity at this point, and his exclusion from the squad against Arsenal proves it.

If Newcastle had known that Jaissle was going to come in and not be a fan of Toure, then there is no way they would have committed such a large fee to bringing him into the club just to be sidelined. It's a huge oversight on behalf of the board, and it's a massive waste of money too.

#105828. How AI is likely to change Germany's job market

How AI is likely to change Germany's job market

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1367 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • At the German government's 2026 Digital Summit in early November, Chancellor Friedrich Merz was asked by a journalist to square a difficult economic circle: If artificial intelligence could make hundreds of thousands of people redundant in the next few years, might it become necessary for the government to give people a basic income to ease the ensuing economic disaster?
  • Surprisingly, Merz didn't respond with a flat dismissal — as might be expected from a conservative politician known for his neoliberal, market-friendly views.
  • It has been revealed that "I've always been a bit cautious about this glitch in recent years," he said, as reported by the news outlet RND.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At the German government's 2026 Digital Summit in early November, Chancellor Friedrich Merz was asked by a journalist to square a difficult economic circle: If artificial intelligence could make hundreds of thousands of people redundant in the next few years, might it become necessary for the government to give people a basic income to ease the ensuing economic disaster?

Surprisingly, Merz didn't respond with a flat dismissal — as might be expected from a conservative politician known for his neoliberal, market-friendly views.

It has been revealed that "I've always been a bit cautious about this glitch in recent years," he said, as reported by the news outlet RND. "However, I'm also well aware that the issue of AI will change our working world so fundamentally that we'll have to give serious thought to many of these challenges in the coming years — including the question: Is our productivity not good enough?".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

What makes this ambiguity notable is that much of Merz's policies since becoming chancellor last year have involved making Germans work more: His government's planned pension reforms would see Germany's retirement age being raised. In July, he unveiled a crackdown on sick leave. And in spring 2025, having barely taken office, he caused much consternation by criticizing the concept of a "work-life balance" and declaring, "We in this country must work more and more efficiently.".

But those policies seem to contradict the impending realities of the labor market in an AI world.

This week, the head of Germany's Federal Employment Agency, Andrea Nahles, warned that the introduction AI would cost Germany as many 800,000 jobs in the next 15 years. Though she also said AI could eventually create a similar number of jobs, clearly the socioeconomic upheaval would be considerable.

It has been revealed that nahles is not the only leading figure concerned about job losses caused by AI. Karsten Wildberger, Germany's minister for digital transformation and government modernization, takes any opportunity he can to warn that Germany must prepare for the economic disruptions of AI.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

And even for Wildberger, a former CEO of a massive retail manufacturer, part of the future economy might come down to giving people free money. He was convinced, he told the Neue Osnabrücker Zeitung in March, "that an unconditional basic income can be part of the solution to cushion the upheavals in the labor market.".

According to recent reports, campaigners have cautiously welcomed this new openness from unexpected quarters. "It shows that in the face of technological transformation we also need to look differently at the question of how we need to secure people's economic stability," noted Kirsten Herrmann, board member at the nonprofit Mein Grundeinkommen (My Basic Income), which runs various projects examining the social and economic impact of universal basic income (UBI).

In a recent development, "But I also think that individual statements by politicians don't amount to a political change, of course," she told DW. "It just means that we need to enter a serious and constructive debate about what kind of a role a basic income can play.".

The idea of a universal basic income is very old: English Renaissance philosopher Thomas More mentions it in his 1516 book Utopia, for instance. But since the 20th century, it has largely been seen as an idealistic notion adopted by leftists — that is, until some of the world's most high-profile tech bosses latched onto the idea as a way to offset the utopian advances they said AI would bring.

Industry observers note that in 2017, Elon Musk, who had co-founded the corporation OpenAI two years earlier, predicted that a universal basic income would at some stage become inevitable. Since then, leading figures in the AI sector, including Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, and Sam Altman, the other founder of OpenAI, have all gone on record in support of UBI (though Altman's interest has cooled somewhat since he launched a massive UBI experiment in the US in 2019).

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In a recent development, but Herrmann said it's a "double-edged sword" when such figures mention the idea. She isn't convinced that organizations like hers and people Elon Musk want the same thing.

"On the one hand, it's always nice when the debate about a basic income gets attention from prominent voices," she remarked. "On the other hand, the basic income that people from the tech business talk about is a kind of neoliberal basic income: They talk about what to do when there are no more profitable jobs for people, because they still actually do need people to do certain things, whereas we talk about a basic income that is meant to give people a secure economic base — before the crisis in the job market happens.".

What makes the comments of Merz and Wildberger all the more eyebrow-raising is that mainstream German economists have long since rejected the basic income idea.

Dominik Enste, director of the democracy, society, and economic ethics department at the German Economic Institute in Cologne, dismissed the idea out of hand — AI or no AI. UBI was, he stated, just too expensive, especially in a country that already has plenty of social welfare costs.

"Many economists have calculated that implementing this in many countries is financially unfeasible — in Germany, for one, simply because of the need to fund commitments that have already been made (including pension payments)," he told DW in an email.

However, he also added: "We will have to change our social security systems if work is replaced by AI and, if necessary, tax AI-generated income. But it will be a conditional basic income that still provides incentives to earn a living.".

In a recent development, other economists are more positive about the idea. "How this plays out depends on many choices we make, and on who makes these choices, in whose interest," mentioned Maximilian Kasy, professor of economics at the University of Oxford and author of a book on the impact of AI on society. "But a lot of the current thrust is to replace workers to increase profits and increase corporate control, though this is not the only path possible.".

According to recent reports, kasy thinks a basic income could be a good solution, "especially if it's financed in a progressive way (so that only those at the lower end of the income distribution are net recipients)," he wrote. "The 'small print' matters very much, though!".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Sources indicate that if the warnings of Wildberger, Musk, Altman et al. are to be believed, AI is already causing a bigger upheaval than any other technological advance in history, partly because of the speed of the innovations, but also because of the scale of the potential impact.

AI innovation is affecting the jobs of the traditional urban middle classes across the entire world. In 2024, the International Monetary Fund predicted that some 40% of employment in the world would be shaped by AI innovations, and as much as 60% in rich, industrialized nations.

It has been revealed that for her part, Herrmann thinks we are not yet asking the truly fundamental questions about the socioeconomic implications of AI: Not just how do we replace the lost jobs and keep the capitalist system going, but what do we actually want to use AI for? As she put it: "Who actually profits when we become more productive through AI? And how do we redistribute that profit to everyone?".

This, she argued, is why there needs to be more debate about how exactly AI is used in the world of work. "Which jobs are going to be replaced by AI is not some law of nature," said Herrmann . "It's something that we can shape politically and socially — and then the bigger question is: Who gets a say?".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • For the first time in 616 days, Tottenham Hotspur have won three Premier League matches in a row.
  • Recent findings suggest that this victory over Crystal Palace was not as impressive as last week’s triumph at Chelsea, but it did not need to be.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the first time in 616 days, Tottenham Hotspur have won three Premier League matches in a row. Three different managers have been sacked in that time, and the mood in north London had plunged to grim lows, but finally there is a sense that something truly exciting is stirring at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Recent findings suggest that this victory over Crystal Palace was not as impressive as last week’s triumph at Chelsea, but it did not need to be. After Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta was sent off in the 13th minute, Spurs simply had to make their numerical advantage count. They did so with relative ease, taking complete control of possession and creating endless goalscoring opportunities.

In a recent development, roberto De Zerbi’s team ended the night with 34 shots to Palace’s two and with 758 completed passes to Palace’s 149. The goals ultimately came from two defenders, Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke, but there was a long list of Spurs players who might have scored here.

It has been revealed that spurs take the lead through an Archie Gray header! ⚪ https://t.co/qSCECkOJur.

In a recent development, did this defeat mark the end for Pierre Sage, the Palace manager? The Frenchman was only appointed in June but it has been a grisly start to the campaign. Palace have the worst defence in the league, have lost six of nine games and have not produced any truly encouraging performances in the Premier League.

Even in the two games Palace have won, against Fulham and Nottingham Forest, they were lucky to do so. The likes of Sean Dyche and Thomas Frank, both of whom would be strong candidates to replace Sage if Palace do pull the trigger, will no doubt have been keeping an eye on events here.

Industry observers note that “I am really aware of the situation,” Sage said. “I don’t like this situation. [But] you can trust in me, I will never give up. I want to be the first on the pitch on Monday. I have the rage to train more. It’s not me to decide this thing [his future]. If I have one hour, I will give my best for one hour. If I have 10 years, I will give my best for 10 years.”.

Recent findings suggest that the decision for Palace chairman Steve Parish, then, is whether this result represented a continuation of the team’s problems or was an aberration caused by the early red card. It would be reasonable for Sage to claim this match was out of his hands from the moment Mateta lunged at Spurs captain Micky van de Ven, but such an argument might not carry much weight with Palace sitting 18th in the table.

Sources indicate that the challenge was foolish in the extreme by Mateta, a player who was much more successful in exiting this game than he has been in his numerous attempts to leave Palace in recent transfer windows. At first glance it did not seem the worst tackle, but the replays were damning: Mateta led with his studs and made forceful contact with Van de Ven’s ankle.

Industry observers note that it was an inexcusably brainless act, after just 13 minutes of play, and the same could be stated of Palace’s defending from a right-wing corner a few minutes later. Mohammed Kudus swirled the delivery to the back post, where Gray was unmarked. Yes, Palace were defending with 10. But no, that does not justify the inability of Sage’s players to spot Gray. Even more embarrassingly, the Tottenham player was unmarked again from another corner shortly afterwards.

It was not the first time this season that Palace’s cause has been undermined by a red card. When they lost at home to Ipswich Town in September, Axel Disasi was sent off after 34 minutes. An absence of discipline? Perhaps. Sage might argue, though, that he is not responsible for his players demonstrating a lack of basic brainpower.

It has been revealed that jean-Philippe Mateta receives his first red card for Crystal Palace! 🟥 https://t.co/U9UYb29mbk.

All of this was welcomed heartily by the Spurs fans, who celebrated Mateta’s dismissal as though it was a goal. Recent results have restored some of the enthusiasm in this corner of north London and the mood here was buoyant, even before Gray’s opener.

“Now we are playing as a team,” De Zerbi mentioned. “Before the international break, we were playing as many good players but not as a team. We showed our maturity. We are improving.”.

The second goal was always coming and it arrived in the 73rd minute, when Van Hecke attacked a wonderful cross by Mateus Fernandes. Palace goalkeeper Dean Henderson saved the first attempt but the ball dropped onto the head of Van Hecke, now seated in the six-yard box, and he happily nodded it home.

Jan Paul van Hecke doubles Spurs' lead! 👊 https://t.co/1Odkkr8wBJ.

The fresh signings at Spurs endured a difficult first few weeks but there were more signs here that they are adjusting to De Zerbi’s system. Sandro Tonali was exceptional in midfield and teenage talent Luca Williams-Barnett also sparkled off the bench. “Tonali was unbelievable,” De Zerbi mentioned. “We played with two players more: Tonali was double.”.

In a recent development, spurs face Leeds United, Ipswich Town, Sunderland and Fulham in their next four league games. The momentum could, and perhaps should, continue to build. Their optimism here contrasted sharply with the angst of Palace, and with the troubled look that was etched on Sage’s face.

It has been revealed that “Very pleased for the performance, very tough game. You don’t know 11 [against 11] would be different game but Crystal Palace are very tough because they defend with a low block, no space and we indicated we are a mature team. Maybe we could score more goals with more nastiness, but I am very happy because we created many chances. We need more goals for sure. It’s not enough, but we are improving a lot.

“I was very nervous before the game, during the game, after the red card, it’s always better playing with one player more. But today, against this team, they played with this behaviour, all behind the line of the ball, aggressive. Very tough game.”.

In a recent development, when asked if Spurs are looking up the table, he replied: “We don’t forget the ambitions. We have to look behind what was the situation two weeks ago. In the last two years, two times 17th in the table, many games without a win in front of our fans. We have to stay focused. They are improving, increasing the level of performance.”.

Recent findings suggest that speaking to Sky Sports, the Palace defender noted: “Definitely was frustrating. It was one of the first tackles of the game. And we felt like we were doing well and it is unfortunate. We go again.

In a recent development, “The main message was don’t concede again, stay tight as a defence and try to hit them on the counter. That is the best initiative when you’re down a man.

Sources indicate that “Unfortunately, it didn’t happen today. We know what we can do as a team, as a back five, the whole unit. There were some positives in the games, but I can’t say much when you lose. We just have to go again.

In a recent development, “Hopefully, the next game we win. The main message is to stay together as a team. We know what we are capable of. It is staying confident and bouncing back.”.

According to recent reports, roberto De Zerbi, the Spurs head coach, had some good news for the supporters on Friday when he said that James Maddison was fit and available despite being taken off at Stamford Bridge. “This week he didn’t work like the other players, but for tomorrow he is available and he is a special player for us. A special player because of the character and he has unique characteristics.

“For James Maddison or the players who are coming from a long injury, they have to work more than the other players, but he has already four or five weeks he is working very hard and consistently.”.

Industry observers note that while Tottenham are chasing a third successive league victory for the first time in 616 day, De Zerbi insisted there will be no complacency. “For me nothing has changed. We started this pre-season with a long project and we have to stay calm and clear in the head to work to build something better than when we came here,” he mentioned. “One win or one defeat more, nothing will change. We have to analyse to improve the results but to improve the results we have to improve all aspects.”.

Industry observers note that pierre Sage, the Palace manager, lightened the load after knocking Fulham out of the Carabao Cup in midweek but seemed surprised that the fans have remained so supportive. “It’s always a good sign,” he said. “I appreciate it [singing his name at Craven Cottage] very much and I can thank them but I prefer they are with the team than me alone. Because I’m the manager, but I’m not the most crucial part of the team, of the performance and the result. I think the players need it more than me but it’s really appreciated from me.”.

Recent findings suggest that asked what he has learnt about fan sentiment from looking at social media, he said: “I think they understood what happened, why we are not perfect at the moment. We don’t care who is the most responsible for the situation. I take the responsibility. I have no problem with that. I just want people to understand what we do and why.”.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League encounter between Tottenham and Crystal Palace.

Last weekend, Spurs enjoyed a historic result, beating Chelsea 2-0 at Stamford Bridge for only the second time in the league for 36 years thanks to Mike Penders’ own goal and Mathys Tel’s stunning solo strike. This result, coupled with the 3-1 victory over Coventry City in their previous home outing, means that Tottenham have won back-to-back league games and are beginning to gather some momentum under Roberto De Zerbi.

Industry observers note that in his pre-match press conference, when asked if he’s felt a change in atmosphere after the triumph at Stamford Bridge, De Zerbi replied: “We have not achieved our goal. We want our fans to be happy, not now, at the end of the season. Now we have to push, we have to stay focused, we have to increase the spirit, the appetite to win games in a row. To do that, we have to show if we are good enough. If we are good enough on the pitch, for sure we are ready. In the head, in the mentality, we have to show, because the step of this club is to win games in a row and to be angry day by day, game by game, win by win. One time or two times are not enough.”.

Palace have endured a tricky and inconsistent start to the season under their summer appointment Pierre Sage, accumulating just seven points from their opening seven league matches while shipping 17 goals. The 1-0 League Cup victory over Fulham in midweek has momentarily eased the pressure on the Frenchman, but given their newfound success in recent campaigns, fan expectations have risen, with recent performances prompting some cause for concern.

Tottenham remain without the suspended Rodrigo Bentancur, while Xavi Simons, Wilson Odobert, Lucas Bergvall, Savio, Tosin Adarabioyo and Mykhaylo Mudryk are out injured. James Maddison was substituted early in the second half at Chelsea with an apparent groin strain, but De Zerbi insists he’s available for this one. Destiny Udogie could also be involved after recovering from a knee problem.

The visitors are without the injured trio of Ismaila Sarr, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chadi Riad, but there’s hope that Quinten Timber and Jorgen Strand Larsen are fit to be involved this evening after they both missed the Fulham victory.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with teams coming shortly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Aston Villa were held to a 0-0 draw against relegation-battling Sunderland on Saturday afternoon, as Unai Emery's side continued their mixed start to the campaign.

The Villans have won just three of their first 11 games in the Premier League this season after the result at Villa Park, leaving them in 11th place in the table, despite having seen the majority of their starting lineup depart during the summer transfer window.

Morgan Rogers joined Chelsea, Youri Tielemans joined Man Utd, Lucas Digne joined Paris Saint-Germain, Ezri Konsa joined Arsenal, Ollie Watkins joined Al-Hilal, and Emi Martinez joined Chelsea, leaving Emery incredibly short of experience and familiarity within his squad.

Emery brought in 10 new players during the summer window to help replace them and strengthen the squad, but the team have struggled to adapt and the results have not been as forthcoming as they would have hoped.

But while Konsa has gone from strength to strength since his move to the Emirates Stadium, establishing himself as one of the best central defenders in the Premier League, the lack of goals in the side has been more of a problem.

Watkins' departure has left a major hole in the side, and while Nicolas Jackson's performances have been largely good, that reliable threat of scoring regularly seems to have gone.

But what is not being spoken about enough is the fact that Aston Villa also allowed Donyell Malen to leave the club permanently in the summer, and he would be the perfect solution to a lot of the issues they are presently having.

The Netherlands international has been in remarkable form since joining AS Roma on an initial loan deal in the January transfer window, scoring 25 goals in Serie A - 12 more than the next-best players in Marcus Thuram and Anastasios Douvikas.

The forward extended his place at the top of that chart with a stunning performance on Saturday night as he scored four goals in their win over Parma, and showed Aston Villa exactly what they are missing in their current side.

“He is strong, inside the area he is devastating.

“He has quickness in his control, in moving the ball, in shooting, and he is composed in front of goal. For us he is an extra weapon. We are keeping him close and we hope he continues like this in these last two matches.”.

When Malen signed for Aston Villa, he had a reputation for being a goalscoring winger with great pace, but Emery seemed to never fully trust him, and ultimately his place in the team was never assured.

Now that he has gone over to Italy, he is showing what could have happened if he had been given that trust. He is scoring goals for fun in a league that is best known for its defensive qualities, and is making it look easy.

If Emery had ever given him that opportunity, then it may be that the sale of Watkins wouldn't have been such an matter. They would have already had a reliable source of goals in the squad, and there would be less pressure on Jackson and youngster Brian Madjo to hit the ground running.

The manager allowed several key players to leave in the summer, but it now seems clear that his biggest mistake was letting Malen leave and not replacing him properly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A former Premier League star who represented both Manchester United and Liverpool has named the club he believes is bigger, offering his verdict on a debate that reveals no signs of going away anytime soon.

The Reds, thanks to the hugely successful managerial reigns of Bill Shankly, Bob Paisley and, more recently, Jurgen Klopp, are the most successful club in English football history, having won a joint-record 20 league titles, as well as twice as many Champions League trophies as their fierce rivals 30 miles east.

However, with the Red Devils enjoying the most dominant period of the modern era, winning 11 league titles under Sir Alex Ferguson during a time when football's commercial landscape was rapidly evolving, the argument from their corner is that they boast more social media followers, a larger global fanbase and, consequently, greater financial muscle in the transfer market, alongside a bigger stadium.

Sources indicate that clearly, this is no open-and-shut case. With plenty of grey areas when it comes to measuring the overall size of a football club, one former player who experienced life at both sides of the divide once attempted to settle the score, even bringing Real Madrid into the conversation for good measure.

Recent findings suggest that paul Ince - one of England's greatest midfielders ever - played 81 times for Liverpool and 281 times for Man United. Revealing his pick for the bigger club out of the two, he remarked, as per All Football:.

"Man United's got to be the biggest club, as much as I love Liverpool. From a historical point of view, Man United with the Busby Babes, all the stuff that's gone on historically.

It has been revealed that from winning trophies... Liverpool had their time with European Cups and that, but I think if you looked at the biggest club, even from a financial point of view, you'd say Manchester United is the club that everybody talks about globally. There's Liverpool, Man United and Real Madrid but the biggest club has got to be Man United.".

Ince played for the Red Devils from 1989 to 1995 under manager Sir Alex Ferguson, helping end the club's four-year trophy drought and 22-year top-flight title wait in the 1992/93 season, which also saw him win the club's Player of the Year award.

A year later, he would help United retain that title, adding to a trophy cabinet that also consisted of a League Cup (1992), and the European Cup Winners' Cup (1991).

Michael Owen is the most famous example of players to have represented both sides. The former Liverpool striker became a household name at Anfield, scoring 158 goals in 297 appearances and winning the Ballon d'Or in 2001. After spells at Real Madrid and Newcastle United, he moved to Old Trafford in 2009, where he spent three seasons, winning a Premier League title in 2010/11.

Other notable players include Peter Beardsley, who played for United early in his career before becoming a Liverpool star in the late 1980s, and Phil Chisnall, who made the controversial move directly from United to Liverpool in 1964.

More recently, Gabriel Heinze was set to play for both clubs, although his proposed move from United to Liverpool in 2007 was famously blocked by Sir Alex Ferguson, with the Argentine instead joining Real Madrid.

There have also been players such as Tom Chorlton, Arthur Riley and Fred Hopkin who crossed between the clubs during earlier periods of their histories.

Inside Gotham FC's move to Icahn Stadium: Debates over pitch quality, fines and the NWSL's logistical struggle
