💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that juan Carlos Amoros is always subtle in demeanor, down to his usual all-black attire, so after Gotham FC's uninspiring 1-0 win over the Seattle Reign on Sunday, his subdued tone was hardly a surprise.
  • Recent findings suggest that "I feel the obligation to almost apologize for the state of the pitch," Amoros mentioned.
  • In a recent development, he was hardly the only one to mention the grass at Sports Illustrated Stadium.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that juan Carlos Amoros is always subtle in demeanor, down to his usual all-black attire, so after Gotham FC's uninspiring 1-0 win over the Seattle Reign on Sunday, his subdued tone was hardly a surprise. His post-match remarks, though, were a departure from the victory lap a coach might take after winning in the NWSL quarterfinals.

Recent findings suggest that "I feel the obligation to almost apologize for the state of the pitch," Amoros mentioned. "I think at this level, in this kind of game, as a league, we should be having a better surface. Unfortunately, our football club did absolutely everything in their power to make sure that was the case. Unfortunately, it wasn't but luckily, it looks like nobody got hurt and the game was what it was.".

In a recent development, he was hardly the only one to mention the grass at Sports Illustrated Stadium. It seeped its way into every post-match media availability, dominated conversation between the players and was a talking point amongst staff working that day. A dull stretch of grass with yellow-green splotches overshadowed one of the most vital matches of the NWSL's season – and put the league on course for an unlikely downsize for Sunday's playoff semifinal between Gotham and the Kansas City Current.

Sources indicate that roughly 24 hours after Amoros' apology, Gotham moved Sunday's game to Icahn Stadium, a 5,000-seater on Manhattan's Randall's Island that they have played at just twice before. Sports Illustrated Stadium, the 25,000-seat venue in Harrison, N.J. that Gotham have called home since 2021, was available but concerns about player safety prompted an unwanted last-minute move.

According to recent reports, "We as a team worked extremely hard to earn a home playoff berth," Gotham captain Tierna Davidson said in a statement on Monday. "What we got was a field that is not the standard this club, this league or our fans deserve. The quality of the game is not up for debate, so we've made the difficult decision to move to Icahn Stadium on Sunday. A smaller stadium means many of you will not be there, and that is the hardest part of this decision.".

Monday's announcement was the final stage of a back-and-forth between Gotham and MLS' Red Bull New York, the primary tenants and operators of Sports Illustrated Stadium, one that highlights the logistical nightmares that have unexpectedly disrupted the NWSL's postseason.

It has been revealed that MLS' World Cup break this summer afforded RBNY the chance to install a fresh pitch at Sports Illustrated Stadium, the process complete by the team's July 25 loss to Charlotte FC. It was the perfect time for a reset ahead of a busy schedule for the new field – 17 other matches were a guarantee, while the potential postseason runs for both RBNY and Gotham meant the number could stretch well over 20 games before the year was over.

In a recent development, by the time Gotham had secured a home quarterfinal with a draw against Angel City on Oct. 4, there was little reason to suspect that the playing surface would become an problem. Matches are rarely relocated because of pitch quality concerns and the field at Sports Illustrated Stadium has historically been one of American soccer's best; it won the Sports Turf Management Association's award for professional soccer fields in 2021, the year Gotham moved in. The NWSL team did not have another home game until Nov. 1, a period in which RBNY played three home games and the stadium hosted a USA Rugby Fall Series doubleheader. Sometime before the early November fixture against the Royals, Gotham raised concerns with their landlords about the field conditions, the scars of the rugby games on Oct. 30 notably visible.

It has been revealed that nothing came of those complaints, though, and so the Royals match went on as scheduled but the conditions did not go unnoticed. The NWSL imposed a $10,000 fine on Gotham for the state of the field, even though they do not manage the venue as secondary tenants. The fine was not widely known – the NWSL Players Association stated it was unaware of the punishment, while a source with knowledge of the matter said RBNY also did not know. Many found out about the fine after Reign head coach Laura Harvey mentioned it in a post-match press conference after the quarterfinal, but worry about the quality of the grass had already reached a fever pitch at that point.

Despite the fine, a field consultant working on the NWSL's behalf inspected the pitch at Sports Illustrated Stadium on Friday and declared that it met FIFA standards. The following day, RBNY hosted their regular season finale against Atlanta United and less than 18 hours later, another group took a look at the field in the hours building up to Gotham's win over the Reign. It was deemed playable on Sunday morning by representatives from the NWSL, the Professional Referee Organization and the NWSLPA, according to a source familiar with the situation.

Industry observers note that even from a distance, the grass appeared problematic. The sand that was left over from the rugby doubleheader still lined the pitch, while some rugby lines were faint but visible in certain spots. The players' review of the surface, though, was damning – Harvey called it "s---," Reign captain Jess Fishlock remarked it was "atrocious," and Gotham midfielder Jaelin Howell described it as "sandy" and "unstable." Gotham attacker Jaedyn Shaw also expressed concern that her planted foot would slip during corner kicks and all agreed that it ultimately impacted the teams' ability to compete.

lower bowl isn’t quite full at kickoff between Gotham and the Seattle Reign, though there are some fans in the upper bowlGotham unveiled earlier that they sold 3,000 tickets through NYC Mayor Mamdani’s offer (including 1,000 in the first 10 minutes of sale)#NWSL pic.twitter.com/qviBM65bsz.

It has been revealed that gotham, in conjunction with the NWSL, spent the hours after their quarterfinal win discussing options with RBNY to improve the playing surface. The main solutions, according to multiple sources, were re-sodding the pitch – essentially ripping the existing field out and installing a latest one – or a hybrid model in which artificial threads would be stitched into the existing grass. Both would be timely endeavors – the former would be longer while the latter might have been completed in time for Gotham to host the Current on Sunday.

There was just one problem. RBNY have a friendly against Club America scheduled for Saturday.

Recent findings suggest that the game will serve as the final match of their season after they missed the MLS Cup playoffs and takes place during the men's international break, which means some players from both teams will be tied up with their national teams instead. Multiple sources said the NWSL could not guarantee that the hybrid model project would not actually be completed in time for RBNY's friendly on Saturday evening, even if it would have been ready in time for Gotham's Sunday afternoon game against the Current. RBNY were unwilling to proceed with the hybrid plan, as a result, and so Gotham chose to leave Sports Illustrated Stadium for Icahn Stadium.

RBNY still intend to play on the pitch that NWSL players complained about on Saturday and no changes to the field are expected to be made beforehand.

Sources indicate that "We understand how frustrating the move is for Gotham and their fans. We had hoped to see Gotham continue its championship run at Sports Illustrated Stadium, too," RBNY remarked in a statement. "We invest in the pitch year-round, with a dedicated grounds team and specialist field partners, and it was cleared for every match played there this season. Those inspections continue for all remaining events this year. We worked closely with Gotham and the NWSL to address their concerns, but unfortunately the experts and the league couldn't guarantee the additional work they wanted to be completed could be done in time. We wish Gotham the best in their match.".

The venue is not brand new to Gotham, who have hosted two games at the stadium in the last two years, and seems well-equipped to at least solve the main problem they faced at Sports Illustrated Stadium. Amoros complimented the quality of Icahn Stadium's pitch when Gotham hosted a Concacaf W Champions Cup group stage game there in Aug. 2025. Though it did not prompt Gotham's selection of Icahn Stadium to host that match, the New Jersey venue's field had also looked suboptimal in the run-up to the continental clash. RBNY subsequently replaced the pitch during that period, weeks before the U.S. men's national team played a friendly against South Korea on Sept. 6 last year.

"I don't really want to talk too much about it but the Sports Illustrated Stadium has traditionally been the best pitch in the league," Amoros said at the time, "and the last couple of games, it's definitely been far away from that so this pitch here is outstanding.".

Gotham's last-minute switch to Icahn Stadium was a surprise in large part because an entirely separate scheduling issue had overshadowed the first week of the postseason.

The NWSL had two broadcast slots for the semifinals, Saturday at noon ET on CBS and Sunday at 3 p.m. ET on ABC, but did not exactly have the first-choice venues to host them. RBNY's Saturday friendly locked Gotham out of that time slot entirely if they wanted to play at Sports Illustrated Stadium, but they needed the Washington Spirit to beat the Portland Thorns for the Sunday window since the Thorns would be unable to hold a game that kicked off at 9 a.m. local time. The Spirit's lopsided win guaranteed Gotham would play on Sunday but they had their own issues – the Secretaries' Cup, a Division III college football game between the United States Merchant Marine Academy and the United States Coast Guard Academy, was taking place at Audi Field during the Saturday time slot.

It has been revealed that the Spirit seemed destined for a semifinal at Northwest Stadium in Landover, Md., home of the NFL's Washington Commanders and a stadium they had never played in before, but late discussions with Audi Field's owners, MLS' D.C. United, and a contribution from sponsor Lafayette Federal Credit Union to underwrite the costs of the schedule change meant that problem was solved.

According to recent reports, gotham's move to Icahn Stadium, though, only reinforced the logistical issues that the NWSL has battled for its entire existence. The optics have favored the league in recent years, with the vast majority of their teams playing in state-of-the-art soccer-specific stadiums and managing to survive the constant game of venue Tetris. Scheduling conflicts, though, were never out of the realm of possibility, and many have marred the league this year. The Boston Legacy, for example, had to move home games from Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Mass. to Centreville Bank Stadium in Pawtucket, R.I., during the World Cup and will play there in 2027 while the construction project continues on Boston's White Stadium.

According to recent reports, the complications that plagued Gotham and the Spirit, though, are in line with a different problem – control over facilities. Around half of the league's teams are secondary tenants in the stadiums they play in, so management of the venues is almost entirely out of their hands. It is unclear how swiftly that will change for any of those teams. Gotham will leave Sports Illustrated Stadium for Etihad Park in 2028, but that stadium will be managed by MLS' Upcoming York City FC. They will continue to be secondary tenants in that building, which technically means they could be subject to the same problems they right now face. MLS' calendar flip next year will likely see the glitch morph but not necessarily change. The leagues' postseason schedules will be different for the foreseeable future but teams like Gotham and the Spirit will still be at the mercy of their landlords in the meantime; Gotham's conflict with RBNY an example of just that. RBNY's friendly was the sticking point in their discussions over the pitch and ultimately took precedence over an NWSL semifinal.

Recent findings suggest that control over venues continues to weigh heavily in the NWSL's expansion process and is a key part of the issue that causes the most hand-wringing in the league's front office – the calendar. The Current might be the NWSL's gold standard as the owners and operators of CPKC Stadium, though they have been hamstrung by the NWSL's scheduling concerns. Kickoff of their quarterfinal win over Angel City was at 11:30 a.m. local time because they were the only team able to take that broadcast slot on CBS. The since-ousted San Diego Wave could not host a game with a 9:30 a.m. local kickoff, while Gotham and the Spirit were locked out of their venues because of MLS matches on the same day.

In a recent development, there is a meet-in-the-middle approach, one that the NWSL might use as often as they can as the expansion process continues. A handful of teams share ownership groups with MLS teams, who chiefly own and operate their own stadiums and tend to treat the NWSL teams as equal tenants. The number will grow in 2028 when teams in Atlanta and Columbus, both owned by the local MLS clubs, will join the league.

#105817. Inside football's Christian revolution: The Premier League stars who say God has saved them from their darkest moments, stopped them diving to win penalties - and why some still face mockery and abuse for their faith

Inside football's Christian revolution: The Premier League stars who say God has saved them from their darkest moments, stopped them diving to win penalties - and why some still face mockery and abuse for their faith

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 20:04 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 05:14 EST, 14 November 2026.
  • When Borussia Dortmund star Felix Nmecha transferred an imaginary crown from his head onto the pitch last weekend, he probably wasn't expecting to spark a firestorm.
  • Industry observers note that arriving at the German national team camp two days later, he was summoned for a grilling by sporting director Rudi Voller and manager Jurgen Klopp.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 20:04 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 05:14 EST, 14 November 2026.

When Borussia Dortmund star Felix Nmecha transferred an imaginary crown from his head onto the pitch last weekend, he probably wasn't expecting to spark a firestorm.

Industry observers note that arriving at the German national team camp two days later, he was summoned for a grilling by sporting director Rudi Voller and manager Jurgen Klopp. His symbol of surrender before God, a goal celebration called ‘The King’s Return’, had blown up into an international news story.

Voller, alongside many of Dortmund’s fans, was concerned by Nmecha's ties to Ballers in God, a network of Christian players founded in 2015 by former Tottenham midfielder John Bostock.

While its core mission is to promote faith in Jesus, the evangelical group is believed to hold a conservative stance on issues such as sexuality and gender – a perspective Nmecha has been in hot water for promoting before.

Recent findings suggest that nmecha insisted that his message was one of love, but as his celebration was dissected worldwide, the furore posed more questions than it answered. What role does the Christian faith play for footballers? What impact is the groundswell of belief having on dressing rooms? And what should teams do when ancient creeds clash with modern culture?

According to recent reports, for months, Daily Mail Sport has been speaking with Christian players, chaplains, and academics. We have found that some footballers are still mocked in dressing rooms for their beliefs. We have also heard tales of elite stars praying with non-League journeymen, and of faith sustaining players through injury crises and rescuing them from dark places after their retirement.

Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha attracted controversy in Germany for his 'The King's Return' celebration against Elversberg last Saturday.

Manchester City winger Jeremy Doku is one of a growing number of practising Christians in the Premier League.

Recent findings suggest that for many players, their beliefs and careers are inextricable. Brentford forward Igor Thiago thinks it was part of God's plan for his father to die so that he would become a footballer and share his beliefs internationally.

It has been revealed that 'If my father were alive, I do not think I would have become a footballer, because I think he wanted me to be someone else,' Thiago tells Daily Mail Sport. 'It wasn’t until later that I understood there was a purpose for me to come here and be someone else. To be Thiago, who is a footballer, who can speak about God for so many people, in another language.'.

According to recent reports, thiago worked as a fruit-carrier, bricklayer, and rubbish collector from the age of 13 in the streets of Gama, Brazil, to provide for his family after his dad passed away. A career in the Premier League was unimaginable back then. Now he is the main man at Brentford and one of several players at the club professing a Christian faith.

And they are not alone in their devotion. Across the top six divisions, 75 per cent of clubs have a Christian in the first team and almost half regularly host Bible studies or prayer meetings, according to a survey of 134 outfits by Christians in Sport.

Sources indicate that their director, Graham Daniels, remembers being told in the 1980s that he was one of just four openly practising Christians in the professional game. An impossible claim to verify, but yes, you read that right, just four. Now you have starting XIs containing more believers than that – and we hear some managers have even been attending church with their squad members. 'There’s a real movement of God within football,' one chaplain at a professional club tells us.

Recent findings suggest that perhaps God is dwelling in the treatment room, too. Bournemouth winger Ben Gannon-Doak has had three major injuries in his career – to his knee, then quad, then hamstring – and credits his growing faith for helping him recover from each blow.

Industry observers note that 'With the first, that was before I was strong in my faith – I didn't cope with that one well. I was 17 and felt lost without being on the pitch,' the 21-year-old tells Daily Mail Sport.

In a recent development, 'The quad injury, I coped better because I started slowly practising my faith more. When my hamstring injury came, I was closer to God than I had ever been before and I coped with that very easily, it was much easier mentally than the other two. I was able to play in the World Cup after that.

Brentford forward Igor Thiago thinks it was part of God's plan for his father to die so that he would become a footballer and share his beliefs internationally.

Arsenal's 'Bible Brothers' are the most famous band of Christian players – around 10 of their stars including 'pastor' Jurrien Timber (left) pray together before matches.

Sources indicate that 'I believe all my injuries happened for a reason and I coped with them the way I did for a reason. I just need to trust God. It makes you stronger, prepares you for things, tests your character. It changes you. Faith has impacted my life in the best way possible.’.

Multiple footballers interviewed for this piece cited the Bible verse Philippians 4:13 – 'I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me' – as a key driver in their life. Gannon-Doak has it tattooed on his left arm.

Football has always had crossover with religion – Manchester City and Everton are among the many clubs to have started as church teams, for example – but the past few years have seen it assume more public prominence.

Recent findings suggest that arsenal's 'Bible Brothers' are the most famous band of Christian players – around 10 of their stars including 'pastor' Jurrien Timber and Noni Madueke pray together in the hotel before matches, and regularly share Bible verses on social media. Organisations such as F3 and Ballers in God, who hold daily prayers and weekly Bible studies, have built Christian fellowship across the divisions.

'Premier League players are on the same call with guys who are semi-pro at step four,' Omar Beckles, a player for League Two Gillingham, tells Daily Mail Sport. 'Lads got together virtually during the pandemic and have been consistently since.' But why the explosion of Christian expression now?

‘An key factor has been the increasing number of players coming from Africa or Latin America, where Pentecostalism and other forms of evangelical Christianity are strong,’ Hugh McLeod, Emeritus Professor of Church History at the University of Birmingham, explains to us.

‘Chaplains interviewed for an academic study in 2011 claimed that elite footballers had “a disproportionate passion for the faith” compared with the average member of society, and they saw the players who had come in from other continents as having a big influence on this.’.

An earlier generation of Christian players graduating into management positions, as well as a broader shift in Gen Z asking the cosmic questions in life, has opened up football to the tender matters of faith. Group Bible studies, or even stoppages for Muslim players to break their Ramadan fasts, were unheard of until recent years.

Sources indicate that 'Christians in a changing room can be frowned upon,' claims Steven Sessegnon, the Fulham academy graduate who now plays for AFC Wimbledon. He was mocked for being baptised.

Marc Guehi was reprimanded by the FA after writing 'Jesus loves you' on Rainbow Laces armbands enforced by the Premier League in support of the LGBTQ+ community.

Daniels, who is now a director at Cambridge United, notes Christian values have earned players respect in the dressing room – and thinks faith could alleviate the turmoil players face when the final whistle blows on their career.

Sources indicate that ‘There was tremendous bullying in the 1980s and 1990s, but the more people saw authentic Christianity, the more they realised that it didn’t harm the changing room, but made it better,' he tells Daily Mail Sport. 'Their integrity shone through – players felt if they talked to Christians, they wouldn’t gossip, and they’d be caring, and they wouldn’t be judgmental.

According to recent reports, ‘In football your identity is achieved. You're as good as your last game. It’s too much pressure for players. That’s why people gamble, drink, and divorce when they retire, because you spent your life having to prove yourself and you don’t know what to do with yourself when you can’t anymore.

In a recent development, 'Or think about the academy players who are released at 16. You were the best kid in your class, then your town, your city, your region, the academy system. Then they are released and disappear from the game. Their identity is shot. They feel shame and failure for the rest of their lives.

'If you know your identity and your purpose is a received gift from God, it’s a complete contrast to everything you’ve ever imbibed. He's going to use your highs and lows in sport to draw you closer to Himself. He’s given you this vocation – this is your gift from Him and He loves you.'.

Sources indicate that beckles concurs. ‘Being a Christian actually gives you an unfair advantage in football because you’re always living with some form of optimism and hope,’ he tells Daily Mail Sport.

‘You know there’s no despair. Setbacks are an opportunity to improve and go again. When my dad died, I really saw God show up. He granted me a level of peace and grace and joy just to function at that time when I was grieving.’.

According to recent reports, that said, there is clearly an occasional tension between faith and football, which can bring fame, wealth, and temptations untold. Pele, for example, was very open about his low-maintenance relationship with Christianity's bedroom bylaws.

Meanwhile, Daily Mail Sport has heard of stars who have felt compelled to switch church after becoming Premier League regulars as they had become too recognised and overwhelmed by their original congregation.

City star Antoine Semenyo has a close relationship with pastor John Thompson and was baptised on a beach in Bournemouth last December.

According to recent reports, then there's the minefield of political and social issues which footballers are scrutinised over. When playing for Crystal Palace in 2024, Marc Guehi was reprimanded by the FA after writing 'I love Jesus' and 'Jesus loves you' on his Rainbow Laces captain's armband, the wearing of which was enforced by the Premier League in support of the LGBTQ+ community.

And that brings us back to Nmecha. He could have simply pointed to the sky, or made a sign of the cross, when celebrating against Elversberg last Saturday. It wasn’t his expression of faith, but rather the specific King’s Return action associated with Ballers in God, which riled a certain crowd. No matter that other players, such as Nottingham Forest's Jair Cunha, have deployed the celebration without incident. Klopp says that after their talks, Nmecha will not be repeating it. Dortmund executives will be breathing a sigh of relief.

In a recent development, the website for The King’s Return campaign initially linked to a live counselling chat run by conservative evangelical organisation Groundwire. There, counsellors espoused the beliefs that homosexuality is sinful and abortion is ‘Satan’s strategy’. When Daily Mail Sport investigated the chat service, we were met with similar views.

According to recent reports, it is not fully clear if Ballers in God agree with Groundwire, or if their members even assume a uniform theological position on such issues, but the network celebrated the scrapping of the Rainbow Laces initiative by the Premier League last year. They appear to have removed the link to the Groundwire chat in the wake of the Nmecha controversy. Daily Mail Sport made repeated requests for an interview with founder Bostock, who has been described as ‘hard to pin down’ and a ‘busy man’, but was turned down.

While high-profile incidents are a PR headache for clubs, there is no need for contrasting moral codes to disrupt a team’s cohesion. ‘You might not agree with someone, but you can respect them and treat them in a non-discriminatory way,’ indicates Dr Keith Parry, Principal Academic in Sport at Bournemouth University.

‘We’ve had openly gay players and referees at the top level in rugby. It is strange that men’s football is different, but questions around sexuality and inclusion go deeper than religion.

In a recent development, ‘There are so many barriers (to players potentially coming out) such as toxic masculinity, fans making homophobic remarks, and so on. There are a lot of Middle Eastern and conservative North American owners in football – how might that impact on inclusion? It depends on the owner.’.

Beckles, who has represented 14 clubs, believes Christian players have a duty to let love rather than division shine through. ‘Footballers are constantly in a world where there’s someone not far from them who will want something from them. Their manager and fans want them to perform, people want their signature, people want them to give them money, their agent wants commercial growth,' he tells us.

Bournemouth and Scotland star Ben Gannon-Doak (right) has the verse 'I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me' tattooed on his left arm.

The young winger credits his faith with helping him through three major injuries.

'It’s nice to meet someone that doesn’t want anything from them and genuinely cares for them eternally. That level of love should set people apart.'.

According to recent reports, despite dressing rooms becoming more tolerant of faith, some players still face derision. 'Christians in a changing room can be frowned upon or mocked,' says Steven Sessegnon, a player for League One side AFC Wimbledon, who was taunted after being baptised while at a previous club.

'You hear some real nasty things. Some boys don’t understand, which we give them grace for. What scares me the most is why people get so worked up about footballers who are believers.

‘We’re not bothering anyone. We’re going about our business in a loving and caring way. It really rubs people the wrong way and it can cause arguments inside the changing room. One boy was told he will never play because he’s too soft, because he’s a Christian.'.

According to recent reports, on matchday, faith is increasingly visible and impacts how players go about their business. The temples are not always glamorous – we hear that some players have even met in the sanctuary of a broom cupboard to squeeze in prayer. Clubs offer what they can. At League One Plymouth, they take the analysis suite – at Arsenal, they have a multi-faith prayer room. Across the pyramid, prayers often ask for protection from injury and the chance to glorify God – but not for a win.

At Championship Charlton, six to eight players read the scriptures and pray together. 'They have God-given talents and want to use them as an act of worship,' states club chaplain Matt Baker, who is also on hand at the training ground on Fridays to pray with players. 'When you see players do the sign of the cross after scoring a goal, they see it as evangelistic, but it's also expressing to God that I'm doing this for you, for your glory.'.

It has been revealed that at Exeter City in League Two, chaplain George Baker tries to spread the love around the club. 'I'll do the rounds of the stadium and chat to the stewards and grounds staff,' he states. 'It's a great opportunity to value the people who are making matchday happen.’.

Beckles indicates that religious considerations even factor on the field. 'How do you live with a level of integrity when you want to win? It’s winning in the right way. The “dark arts” are really difficult to navigate,’ he tells Daily Mail Sport, and he is not the only player to express this feeling to us.

'Being a Christian actually gives you an unfair advantage in football because you’re always living with some form of optimism and hope,' says Omar Beckles (right).

Industry observers note that ‘In my heart of hearts, I’d like to think I wouldn’t dive to win a penalty – that’s deception. I try my best not to do any of that. But there is the heat of the moment that exposes our nature.’.

According to recent reports, gannon-Doak adds: ‘Players losing their temper, starting fights, that's the stuff I try to avoid. But some of the dark arts, that’s just part of the game.’.

A popular Christian slogan since the 1890s goes as follows: ‘What would Jesus do?’ Typically it is applied to quandaries in a believer’s life – how to treat somebody who has seriously wronged you, for instance.

In a recent development, not as often has it been wondered: ‘Would Jesus go down if a sweaty centre-back tugged his shirt in the penalty box in the 90th minute?’ But the next time you catch a game, you might just catch an athlete wrestling with that kind of question. What would you do?

To read more about the relationship that Brentford players have with their faith, see here.

Industry News: Germany news: Germany holds national day of remembrance

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, this live blog is now closed. Read on for a roundup of the top stories from and about Germany on the weekend of November 14-15, 2026:.

Thank you for reading this weekend's Germany news blog.

Sources indicate that we'll bring you more from the heart of Europe on Monday. We wish you a very Schönen Abend!

Austrian President Alexander Van der Bellen has urged Europeans to defend compassion and humanity during Germany's national day of mourning for victims of war and oppression.

Speaking at a ceremony in the Bundestag in Berlin, Van der Bellen warned against becoming desensitized to suffering despite the constant images of war and violence.

"Compassion is not a weakness; it is a human strength; it is the foundation of humanity," he stated.

He also addressed the responsibility of later generations for the crimes of the past.

Although people today bore no personal guilt for their ancestors' actions, he noted, they were responsible for what they learned from history and how they treated others.

"Let us ensure that our home, Europe, remains a place where people can live in peace, freedom and dignity," he said.

Bundestag President Julia Klöckner also called for the defense of democracy, pointing to Ukrainians risking their lives to protect freedom.

Germany's Volkstrauertag commemorates soldiers and civilians killed in war, as well as victims of Nazi persecution and other forms of oppression.

German police have arrested three suspects after thieves rammed a car into a jewelry store in the Bavarian city of Bayreuth and stole valuables worth around €10,000 ($11,600).

Bavarian Interior Minister Joachim Herrmann noted the stolen items included jewelry and silver coins.

The burglars drove a car into the store early in the morning before fleeing in a second vehicle, police said.

Officers spotted the getaway car on the A9 highway and gave chase. The suspects left the highway near Weidensees, abandoned their vehicle beside a wooded area and fled on foot.

Police debuted a search involving patrol cars, dogs, drones and a helicopter.

All three suspects were subsequently arrested, with some of the stolen goods recovered.

Prosecutors are expected to decide whether to seek pretrial detention for the suspects.

Detroit Lions receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown played his first NFL American football game in Germany in Munich.

St. Brown made his professional debut in Germany as the Detroit Lions faced the New England Patriots at Munich's Allianz Arena. The 27-year-old grew up in Southern California, and his mother, Miriam, is from Leverkusen. Both his parents were due to watch from the stands.

The NFL player spent childhood summers with his grandparents in the Rhineland.

"This is awesome. A dream come true," St. Brown mentioned before the game. Asked by German broadcaster RTL what he had been looking forward to most, he reeled off a list that included schnitzel, potato dumplings, sauerkraut, currywurst and fries with mayonnaise.

"I'm really excited. I can't wait," he mentioned. "Being in Germany with my teammates and my family — I want to enjoy it and take it all in.".

Two people were slightly injured after an unidentified man threw a firework into the entrance of a gay bar in Frankfurt, police mentioned.

The attack took place at the Zum Schwejk bar, a venue popular with the city's gay community, on Saturday evening.

Police said the bar was clearly identifiable as an LGBTQ+ venue because of a rainbow flag displayed outside.

The motive remains unclear, and police have not said whether they suspect a homophobic attack.

Officers are investigating suspected aggravated assault and have appealed for witnesses.

It has been revealed that the bar said it was "shocked and stunned" by the incident and apologized to guests who witnessed it. It said it wanted to be a place where everyone felt welcome, respected and safe, and pledged to do everything it could to prevent a repeat.

Andreas Ewald, LGBTQ+ policy spokesperson for the Greens in the Hesse state parliament, condemned the attack and called for those responsible to face the full force of the law.

He also urged the state government to establish a roundtable on LGBTQ+ safety involving community representatives, police and victim support organizations.

The bar's name refers to a Czech soldier in the satirical anti-war novel "The Good Soldier Svejk.".

Police in Berlin have filed 28 criminal charges against demonstrators who marched throught the capital on Saturday as part of the Gen Z regelt (Gen Z Takes Charge) movement.

Some 1,200 demonstrators took part in the march, although only 100 had registered for the event under German laws regulating public protests.

The protesters complained about dilapidated schools, the threat of compulsory military service, cuts to university and social funding and other issues.

In a recent development, police mentioned there had been some clashes with participants. A police spokeswoman said the criminal charges were filed for riot, assault, resisting officers and violations of explosives regulations.

Three police officers of the 700 deployed to ensure securty were injured during the demonstration.

November 20 is likely to see more large protests in both Germany and Europe, with some 15,000 demonstrators registered for a march in Berlin.

German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier has expressed solidarity with the Jewish community in Germany amid what he described as ever "louder and more aggressive" antisemitic voices.

Speaking at the presentation of the Prize for Understanding and Tolerance awarded by the Jewish Museum in Berlin, Steinmeier noted: "For all those to whom our country, its constitution and the values it enshrines mean something, there can be only one answer to such antisemitism: to stand side by side with Jewish people in our country.".

Steinmeier noted he deplored the frequent vandalism of memorials to Nazi crimes.

"I am profoundly ashamed of that all," he stated, saying that anyone who mocked the work of museums and memorial sites or collectively blamed, threatened and attacked Jews "attacks the heart of our republic.".

The president also congratulated the prize winners — German journalist and author Düzen Tekkal and British philanthropist Michael Moritz — on their awards.

In a citation, the museum described Tekkal as a champion of human rights who consistently opposed antisemitism and racism while promoting interfaith dialogue, equality in education and opportunities, peace and democracy.

The museum commended Moritz for supporting artistic projects that show Jewish perspectives and strengthen social dialogue.

The Jewish Museum, which is marking its 25th anniversary this year, has been presenting the prize since 2002.

Some 600 sheep have made their way through the southern city of Nuremberg on their way to western winter pasturage, watched by crowds of spectators.

The sheep follow an around 10-km-long (6-mile-long) route that crosses a number of streets and the market square.

The annual event is meant, among other things, to draw attention to the tradition of transhumant, or itinerant, sheep-keeping in the region and the benefits the animals have for landscape conservation.

"With their grazing in summer, sheep create great biodiversity in many key biotopes in the urban region," the city of Nuremberg remarked ahead of the migration.

Thieves have stolen several valuable items from a jewelry shop in the southern city of Bayreuth after ramming it with a car, police noted on Sunday.

They said a black Mercedes carrying three people crashed into the shop in the early hours of Sunday morning.

The burglars then fled the scene in a second Mercedes, this time a gray one, after taking a number of articles.

The getaway car was then spotted by a police patrol on a motorway heading south, with officers setting off in pursuit.

Events are taking place around Germany for the Volkstrauertag (people's day of mourning), a day on which armed forces personnel and civilians who died in armed conflicts and victims of violent state oppression are commemorated.

Austrian President Alexander Van der Bellen is to speak in the parliament at the main commemoration ceremony of the German War Graves Commission at midday.

His presence reflects the large number of Austrians who were killed in action in the Second World War while fighting for the German Wehrmacht following the annexation of their country by Nazi Germany in 1938.

German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, the patron of the commission, will also hold a speech and lay a wreath.

Last year, Steinmeier decreed that the Volkstrauertag should also commemorate people who were persecuted and killed by the Nazis because of their sexual identity, as well as police officers who have lost their lives in the course of duty.

There will also be a remembrance ceremony at the Jewish Cemetery in Berlin for those of the Jewish faith killed in World War I.

In remarks to the DPA news agency ahead of the remembrance day, the speaker of the lower house of German parliament, or Bundestag, Julia Klöckner, called on society to actively defend democracy.

Klöckner said that the Volkstrauertag was a reminder of how destructive tyranny and contempt for human dignity can be.

Industry observers note that "Democracy is the antidote here," she remarked. "But it is not an heirloom. It wastes away when we do not constantly renew its promise of basic rights and freedom.".

You join us as Germany holds a day of remembrance for the victims of war and oppression and also commemorates members of the police force killed while carrying out their duties.

Industry observers note that but why does Germany need these powers now? And how far can its secret services go in a country with a history of strict limits on intelligence operations?

Published: 06:01 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 11:56 EST, 18 November 2026.

When most footballers are recovering from a serious injury, the stadium is the last place they want to be. If the team are winning, they feel left out. In difficult times, they feel helpless and frustrated. So the best thing to do is stay away and avoid even watching matches on TV.

According to recent reports, amadou Onana is different. The Aston Villa midfielder has not played since sustaining a serious knee injury during Belgium’s last-16 tie with the United States at last summer’s World Cup and still has some way to go before he can feature again.

Still Onana is playing his part. Dressed in eye-catching clothes, he is often pitchside at Villa Park before and after matches, geeing up the crowd or offering advice and encouragement to younger team-mates. He does the same in the dressing room, where his command of five languages is invaluable. To help upcoming goalkeeper Zion Suzuki settle, Onana is trying to learn basic Japanese.

Villa have missed Onana this season and this week indicated their faith in him by handing the 25-year-old a two-year contract extension through to 2031 on Wednesday – a rare gesture to a man who will not play again for some time.

‘It’s a substantial one for me,’ claims Onana, taking a break from his recovery to speak to Daily Mail Sport in Villa’s giant indoor training facility known as ‘The Barn’.

‘When I got injured during the World Cup, (director of football) Damian Vidagany came all the way to Los Angeles to see me. They revealed massive faith in my ability and who I am as a person.

Aston Villa midfielder Amadou Onana has signed a new five-year contract, extending his existing deal by two years and committing his future to the club alongside manager Unai Emery.

It's a show of faith in the Belgian, who has been absent since suffering a serious knee injury at the World Cup.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Very few players renew their contract while they’re out with such a serious injury, so it’s very gratifying. As for the recovery, it’s going to strategy.

‘The start is the hardest bit. Now I’m back on my feet, in the gym and moving weights so I feel like myself again. I’m happy with how it’s going.

‘There is no precise timeline. It’s just a question of seeing how I’m progressing. I’m pretty chilled about it and I know I have to take my time because with such a serious injury, if you come back too early you might re-hurt yourself.

‘Not many people talk about it but football can be lonely in some aspects. I know we earn a lot of money and do an incredible job, and I’m very grateful for it.

Recent findings suggest that ‘But there are downsides to it that people have to bring to light. If you go home and it’s total silence – just you and you – it can be very complicated. Throughout my injury, it’s a lonely and dark place at times. Luckily the family and the people around me make a huge difference.’.

Industry observers note that onana is an unusual modern footballer. Coaches regularly complain about how few vocal leaders there are among the current generation yet Onana is never afraid to speak up.

He first wore the captain’s armband for Belgium at 21, after Kevin De Bruyne was substituted during a friendly against Germany in March 2023.

It has been revealed that villa need those qualities more than ever. Last summer they lost Emi Martinez, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne, Morgan Rogers and Ollie Watkins, who were all notable in the dressing room. Even though skipper John McGinn is still around, this is a latest Villa and some of their performances this season have reflected that lack of experience.

A summer exodus of experienced players means Onana's leadership is more key than ever at Villa.

‘Going to the stadium for the first time wasn’t easy at all,’ Onana admits. ‘Even now when I’m watching games and I can’t help my team-mates, it’s frustrating. But I understand my responsibility at this club as well.

According to recent reports, ‘I’m not a "young talent" any more. I am part of the leadership group with Belgium and I know what that means. We have plenty of major personalities and leaders but whenever they need me, I show up.’.

Sources indicate that communication certainly helps. Onana was born in Dakar, Senegal, and grew up speaking Wolof, the most widely spoken language in that country. He has also mastered French, Dutch, German and English.

‘Because I’m not in the dressing room all the time, I have an outside perspective on it,’ Onana explains. ‘I am into one-to-one talks, making sure everyone feels OK and comfortable within the team.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I can speak to Johan Manzambi, Nicolas Jackson, Ibrahim Mbaye and Modou Keba Cisse in French, and I was pleased we signed Leon Goretzka so I can speak to him in German and maintain my level. Japanese is the next one.’.

The messages Villa players really need to heed, though, are the ones Emery delivers.

Players rarely have it easy during their early weeks at Villa. Rogers adapted almost instantly after joining in January 2024 but he is the exception that proves the rule.

Sources indicate that ‘He made me feel uncomfortable,’ Onana recalls. ‘He took me into areas where I wasn’t ready to go and revealed me aspects of my game I needed to be better at.

Industry observers note that ‘He has challenged me over and over again in training and games, and he’s made me a better player, certainly on the ball. He doesn’t care about losing the ball or making a mistake. He wants me to be brave and play.’.

‘He has challenged me over and over again in training and games, and he’s made me a better player,' says Onana of Emery.

The working relationship should continue for some time yet. Emery revealed earlier this month that he had discussed a upcoming contract with Villa co-owner Nassef Sawiris, which would likely make him one of the two highest-paid Premier League managers along with Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta.

The start to this season has been bumpy at times but Onana is convinced Villa are on the right track.

‘Unai Emery is the best manager I’ve had and we are lucky to have him,’ states Onana. ‘(Emery's possible new contract) is a massive one for the players, staff and fans.

‘He played a massive part in me renewing my contract as well which shows the faith and belief he has in me. What he’s done here, not many managers have done it.

Sources indicate that ‘We’ve played in Europe four seasons in a row now. We won the Europa League last year. He’s creating a culture that I’ve never seen before. Now we are asking ourselves what else we can achieve. He pushes us to the limit and it seems to work.’.

It has been revealed that onana, you sense, needs to keep himself busy. There is not much peace at home these days: his son recently turned one and keeps his parents on their toes, especially as he has just learned to walk. ‘It’s the best job in the world,’ Onana reflects.

All things being equal, Onana should have at least a decade left as a player but he is already considering the next steps and is studying for his UEFA B coaching licence.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I think it can make me a better player and give me a better understanding of how coaches see the game,' he says. 'A coach’s job is underestimated. People can’t fathom the time it takes or how much thinking you have to do just to prepare a training session.

‘I’ve been working with 16-to-17-year-olds and it’s a heck of a challenge. It’s pretty interesting trying to work out what coaches are thinking and why they initiative certain sessions.’.

Onana's son recently turned one and keeps his parents on their toes. ‘It’s the best job in the world,’ he reflects (Source: Instagram/its_onana).

In a recent development, emery has long been a master at this and demands total commitment. Many times he has urged his players to think solely about their careers, with other considerations coming later.

In a recent development, onana could not have reached this level without serious dedication, yet he appreciates that life exists outside football. ‘There were times last season where I would see my wife only twice a week due to all the travelling,’ he reveals.

Sources indicate that ‘Now I can blueprint my weeks. Sometimes I can plan a weekend away, be a dad, be a husband. That’s crucial too. It’s all about balance. Too much of something is never good. I don't think a plumber goes out in the day, works and then comes home and tries to do some plumbing at home.

It has been revealed that ‘If I’m only remembered as a footballer, then I will have failed. Football is my job and I'm very, very dedicated to it, but it's not what defines me. I’m trying to make a positive impact in the world in very different aspects. When I’m gone, that’s what I want people to remember from who Amadou Onana was.’.

Despite restrictive abortion laws, Poland's 'Abortomat' — a locker that dispenses abortion pills — helps women who want to end a pregnancy

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1192 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Women's rights activists in Poland have opened what they say is the world's first delivery locker supplying abortion pills in a country with one of Europe's most restrictive abortion laws.
  • Known as the "Abortomat," the locker is in a building opposite the Polish parliament, in what activists say is a clear message to politicians like Donald Tusk.
  • Only two European Union member states, Poland and Malta, do not allow abortion on request.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Women's rights activists in Poland have opened what they say is the world's first delivery locker supplying abortion pills in a country with one of Europe's most restrictive abortion laws.

Known as the "Abortomat," the locker is in a building opposite the Polish parliament, in what activists say is a clear message to politicians like Donald Tusk. The Polish prime minister pledged to introduce abortion on demand up to the 12th week of pregnancy before the 2023 parliamentary election, but his coalition has been unable to agree on a common position.

Only two European Union member states, Poland and Malta, do not allow abortion on request.

In Poland, abortion is only allowed when the pregnancy is the result of a crime — rape or incest — or when it endangers the health or life of the woman.

Justyna Wydrzynska, an activist from a nonprofit organization called Abortion Dream Team, demonstrated DW the "Abortomat" in a small room behind a tasseled portiere at Abotak, Poland's first abortion center.

Inside, the pink lighting is subdued. Glitter tassels, baubles and spotlights make it feel a bit like a disco, she stated.

Recent findings suggest that the "Abortomat," which opened in late September, has 22 pink lockers. To open one, a woman receives a PIN code from the organization Women Help Women after completing a medical questionnaire, which is then checked by a doctor.

Sources indicate that parcel lockers have sprung up like mushrooms after rain in Poland in recent years. Even the smallest villages have them.

Industry observers note that "When you walk around Poland, vending machines are everywhere. This is our culture. People in the US have Amazon, we have vending machines for everything," said Wydrzynska.

Women in Poland who have an abortion are not criminalized. But anyone who helps them terminate a pregnancy risks up to three years in prison.

Sources indicate that in 2023, Wydrzynska was the first activist to be convicted in Poland of helping a woman to have an abortion by sending her pills. The conviction was later overturned, and the court ordered a retrial.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Inside each compartment at the "Abortomat" is a package that normally contains two drugs, mifepristone and misoprostol, usually taken up to the 14th week of pregnancy.

It has been revealed that because mifepristone is not registered in Poland, the drug must be ordered from abroad where it is legal. Information on how to do this is not easy to come by, which is where Abortion Dream Team and Abotak come in. They help women find information about accessing medication, which is sent from abroad by Women Help Women, or help them to travel abroad for a termination.

Wydrzynska said she believes the "Abortomat" does not break the law because it is a machine, not a person, that is delivering the pills, although she admits she is not sure.

Recent findings suggest that dr. Sabrina Mana-Walasek, a reproductive rights lawyer representing Wydrzynska, remarked the legal environment for abortion pills is "complicated.".

She said that although mifepristone is not registered in Poland, it is registered in the European Union and, as EU citizens, Polish women can order it and take it.

"If a woman orders pills for herself and pays for them herself, it's not a crime," she stated.

The ultra-Catholic legal group Ordo Iuris disagrees and has notified the prosecutor's office that the activists are committing a crime.

"In the case of an 'Abortomat,' the actions enabling a woman to have an abortion are theoretically performed by the woman herself using the device, but the reality is that this machine is operated by people — they send the code required to open the compartment containing abortion pills, they order and procure the pills, and they restock the compartments," said Katarzyna Gesiak, director of the Ordo Iuris Center for Medical Law and Bioethics.

Wydrzynska said anti-abortion activists regularly demonstrate outside Abotak, using horns and loudspeakers to generate loud noise to annoy the center's residential neighbors and pressure the landlord to revoke their rental agreement.

At one demonstration, a woman holding an image of the Virgin Mary told DW she believes abortion "is the work of Satan.".

"Abortion is evil, it's demonic, it's against the fifth Commandment, 'Thou shalt not kill,'" she mentioned.

It has been revealed that earlier this year, Diana, a 25-year-old Ukrainian woman living in Warsaw, used abortion pills during her sixth week of pregnancy before the "Abortomat" started up. She got the pills using information provided by Abortion Dream Team.

Diana told DW that she has never wanted to have children.

Industry observers note that "I was expecting something like a headache, stomachache, maybe vomiting, but I had nothing like that. It was just like a normal period. I didn't feel any pain. It was really easy for me," she remarked.

Sources indicate that "I felt relief because I knew that it was the right choice for me. I knew that I can live my life," she added.

Another Abortion Dream Team activist, Natalia Broniarczyk, stated they help about 130 women daily in Poland. About 125 of these women use pills that cost about €75 ($83), while the remainder travel to a clinic abroad.

In contrast, just 851 abortions were performed in Polish hospitals last year.

Broniarczyk is concerned about the rising support for right-wing parties ahead of next year's parliamentary election, but she's also furious at the inactivity of liberals in Tusk's coalition.

In a recent development, "I'm mad at the liberals because for three years, they did nothing to protect us. They lost three years and now, when we're close to an election, they are fighting for our voices and respect. People are more progressive than politicians," she stated.

After taking office in 2023, Tusk's coalition, which includes left-wing and conservative partners, were unable to agree a common position and their separate bills failed to obtain parliamentary approval in 2024.

Afterwards, Tusk stated abortion on request would not be possible during the current parliamentary term.

In October, however, two bills were resubmitted to the Sejm, the lower house of parliament, and were narrowly approved.

Sources indicate that one reinstates severe irreversible fetal defects as a justification for a legal termination. This justification had been ruled illegal by the Constitutional Court in 2020 when the previous right-wing Law and Justice (PiS)-led government was in power.

The 2020 ruling led to tens of thousands of people, mostly women, taking part in street protests in towns and cities across the country, some of the largest since communism fell in 1989.

Lawmakers also approved a bill partially decriminalizing anyone who helps a woman terminate her pregnancy.

According to the results of a recent poll conducted by SW Research for Onet.pl, almost 61% of respondents said they want the country's right-wing president, Karol Nawrocki, who is backed by PiS, to sign into law the bill on the fetal defect justification.

Nawrocki opposes abortion, and both Wydrzynska and Broniarczyk think he will use his power of veto to block the bills, preventing them from becoming law.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While no one has officially confirmed that Mauricio Pochettino is departing the United States men's national team for Manchester United after Michael Carrick's sacking, the faces of Sebastian Berhalter and Folarin Balogun mentioned everything that you needed to know at media availability on Thursday ahead of their Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals match with Haiti. With a spot in the Nations League final at stake in this competition, there's a need to be professional during this, and they stressed that, but it was also hard to hide emotions when the manager under whom they experienced some of their best times as USMNT internationals and an entire World Cup is about to depart.

When asked about what he wanted to see, Balogun was succinct, saying, "If I had a vote, I would like to keep things the way they are.".

He continued, saying, "I think things have been working well; we have a clear sense of identity, we have a clear playing style, and whenever you have a top coach, you'd want him to stay, as it's a no-brainer, so I think for us it's no different.".

Industry observers note that it's hard not to feel for Balogun after he became the story of the World Cup for the wrong reasons, with his red card rescinded before he played against Belgium in the round of 16, where the USMNT suffered a 4-1 loss, crashing out of the tournament. Then things went from bad to worse when his move to Everton was called off due to a change in contract terms, and now he is struggling for playing time at Monaco. While he still prepares to leave the French club in January, the national team camp was supposed to be an escape, but instead it has become another uncertain period as Pochettino's days come to an end. Berhalter confirmed that the team hasn't officially heard anything, but that their focus is still on the game at hand.

"We're focused on going against Haiti twice; they're a good team. You saw at the World Cup, they surprised people, so that's our main focus, and I think the group is ready to play these games," Berhalter said.

It has been revealed that date: Saturday, Nov. 14 | Time: 4:30 p.m. ETLocation: Nu Stadium -- Miami, FloridaTV: TBS | Live stream: HBO MaxOdds: Haiti +750; Draw +440; USMNT -350.

Recent findings suggest that berhalter made his national team debut under Pochettino and hasn't looked back, securing 22 caps for the team and making it hard for the Argentine to decide how he should set up the midfield. Because of that, it's hard not to be reflective in uncertain times like these.

In a recent development, "Personally, on the field and off the field, he's done a lot for me, and from day one he's always believed in me. Before I set foot on the field, I think about the way I play and the way that I try to carry myself," Berhalter said. "He just said it doesn't matter what you're doing on the field; these are already the right things. And to be honest, I can't thank him enough, and regardless if he's coach, not the coach and, I say it every time that he's meant so much to me. And he's helped me develop as a player and as a person, and as a player, that's all you can ask for: to have that trust and have that belief in you. And for me, it's easy to go out there and just do my job so, he's meant a good deal to me for sure.".

In a recent development, this is all tough to manage while having games to play. Sure, players will say they're going to be professionals, and these are people who have dealt with stress and needed to maintain that professionalism while doing so, but from a human perspective, it's a well-liked coach leaving on short notice. Even if people anticipated that Pochettino might not make it through to the 2030 World Cup and his departure was a sign that a coach who has done well at the helm was leaving, that doesn't make it any easier on the players. If they go ahead quickly against Haiti on Saturday, they could turn the match into a celebration of what has been so great while playing for Pochettino, but going behind can have a cascading impact where doubt starts to creep in. It's something that the USMNT will need to avoid, even if the future is bright for this squad, no matter who is coaching them.

It has been revealed that pochettino helped raise the standard, and with young players like Cavan Sullivan, Adri Mehmeti, Matias Albert, Neil Pierre and Julian Hall, the future is already here, and no one can feel complacent about their spots. These are things that the upcoming coach can bring in, and Pochettino's leadership can set a new standard of what to look for.

"Yeah, I think the benefit and the blessing when you have a great coach is you know the standard," Balogun noted. "I think Poch definitely raised the standard since he's been in charge. I think you guys have seen that, just the intensity of training, how we approach games, he's changed our way of thinking as players, from calling the friendlies that we have in certain camps official games, not official games. He wants us to just be of a mindset to go out there and win.".

"He's laid the foundation, and I think we, as players, have that ownership to not just do that because Poch was in charge; I think we have the ownership as players to carry that out because we know the standard," he continued. "So yeah, I think that's the benefit of having a top coach, and I'm sure you know whether he's here or not, the US will look to replace him with another top coach.".

Who succeeds Pochettino will be vital, but what the players have learned from his time will be invaluable, so the standard can't slip from here. As Balogun said, it's time to take ownership of their own future because while the coaches may change, the players tasked with leading this team back to the top of Concacaf are already here and understand the task at hand.

Juventus coach Luciano Spalletti insists the only way to avoid growing speculation about Antonio Conte’s potential return is to ‘win matches’ as the Bianconeri prepare to host Venezia in Serie A.

It kicks off at 12:30 CET [11:30 GMT] at the Allianz Stadium in Turin.

Juventus have won only two of their last five league matches, earning a 1-1 draw against Fiorentina before the international break.

Venezia are in the relegation zone, but have won two of their last five, both under upcoming coach Davide Nicola.

Edon Zhegrova starts for the first time in Serie A, joining Kerim Alajbegovic and Randal Kolo Muani in the Juventus attack, while Nick Woltemade begins on the bench.

“Given our name and the players we have, there are options. We need to keep our balance and be wary of counterattacks, because that’s what they rely on,” Spalletti told DAZN minutes before kick-off.

“[Davide] Nicola has got them well organised and always finds new solutions, so we’ll need to be patient, maintain our balance, and be creative in our decisions.”.

Former Juventus coach Conte has openly admitted that he’d like to return to Juventus one day. Spalletti already commented on Conte’s claims on Saturday, and today he was asked whether he wanted to add something more.

“I don’t want to add anything; I just want to focus on winning today,” he replied.

“When you manage Juventus, if you don’t want all the talk swirling around you, you just have to win matches. All of this is quite normal when you reach a level where you’re on TV every day.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki went from being serenaded with a chorus of “world’s No 1” to making a bizarre blunder that denied Unai Emery’s side a third successive Premier League victory.

The Villa manager, however, preferred to focus on a string of important saves from Suzuki rather than the uncharacteristic mistake that allowed Fulham to collect a deserved point.

It all went wrong for the hosts just after the hour mark in a match where Fulham provided more than a few scares before finding the net in unexpected fashion.

In a recent development, alex Iwobi, who had been denied superbly by a Suzuki save just moments earlier, swung in a corner. It was right on top of the Villa goalkeeper, who tried to keep it out but only succeeded in fumbling it over the line. A frantic attempt to gather the ball was in vain and goal-line technology confirmed the goal stood.

In a recent development, zion Suzuki drops Alex Iwobi's corner and Fulham are level! 🫨 https://t.co/KwLFMRpKqk.

Suzuki appeared to have been put off by the presence of Fulham’s Shea Charles, but Emery refused to single out the player for criticism.

“I prefer to speak about the saves that he made,” the Villa manager remarked. “This is part of football. I think he played fantastically and he is doing a lot of saves so he can make one mistake. It is part of football. We can be mature about this.

According to recent reports, “I still want to see consistency. Over the last five Premier League matches, we are winning three and drawing two. It’s not bad but with our poor start it’s not enough.

“We have to change our mind quickly for Tuesday against Barcelona. We want to test ourselves at this level.”.

Villa go to the Nou Camp with a 100 per cent Champions League record to their name this season. But they will need to improve on Saturday evening’s performance to get a result in Spain.

As well as Suzuki’s error, a 14th-minute penalty miss from John McGinn also proved costly.

The Japanese international is Villa’s own version of former Manchester City goalkeeper Ederson, who revolutionised English football with a vast range of passing from his own penalty area.

Of all the daft statements to have come out of Aston Villa – and I am including Doug Ellis’s frequent claims that he invented the bicycle kick – it is hard to think of anything as absurd as suing a pundit for speaking the truth.

Jamie Carragher’s common-sense declaration that Villa manager Unai Emery might consider a move to Manchester United – because it is a bigger club – has apparently inflicted such a deep wound to the self-esteem of Nassef Sawiris, the chairman, that he has initiated a legal complaint.

Sources indicate that sawiris’s short statement, which he published on social media on Friday night, consisted of 37 ill-chosen words. The 31-year-old joined Villa on a free transfer in the summer, but a knee injury prevented him from making an appearance off the bench until this month’s Champions League tie against Fenerbahce.

Asked what role Goretzka would have with Villa, Emery deadpanned: “The first one is to be available to play.”.

Tonight sees a battle between two Spaniards at Villa Park as Aston Villa host Fulham. Both sides are looking to bounce back from disappointing midweeks having been knocked out of the League Cup; Aston Villa lost 3-0 at Bournemouth, while Fulham fell to a 1-0 defeat at home against Crystal Palace.

After a slow start to the season in the league, Aston Villa’s form has picked up, which includes handing Manchester City their first defeat of the season a week ago. After this evening, Aston Villa have games against Barcelona and Manchester United before the international break but Unai Emery has insisted his full focus is on this game.

“If we are thinking after the match against Fulham, then we are making a mistake and we are completely wrong,” Emery said. “We are prioritising the Premier League, and this is the message. To keep our consistency and demands means that each match is a test.”.

Having failed to win any of their first six league games, Fulham have now won back-to-back Premier League games, with consecutive 1-0 wins over Hull and Coventry, which has lifted them out of the relegation zone.

Sources indicate that “It [managing in England] is a very tough challenge but I am so happy to be here,” Alvaro Arbeloa mentioned. “I am where I want to be and I am really enjoying my days. I want to win games and I think we are performing well but we need to improve.

“They [Aston Villa] are very compact, they defend so well and even with the ball they know what they have to do. And they have top players, and when you have a top coach with top players, normally you have a top team. I think right now he [Unai Emery] is one of the best coaches in the world. He is very, very good, he improves everything every year. It does not matter where he is coaching, he is doing an amazing job, and for me also it is a very good challenge to face him.”.

In the two league meetings between these sides last season, it was one win apiece; Aston Villa won this fixture 3-1 just over a year ago before Fulham won 1-0 at Craven Cottage back in April. Team news from Villa Park to follow shortly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Napoli coach Massimiliano Allegri claims Antonio Vergara’s injury might be related to the ‘greater pressure’ the Italian talent is facing this season and insists the Partenopei must be ‘realistic’ in their next Champions League game against Manchester City.

Vergara suffered a new muscle injury on Saturday night, during Napoli’s 1-0 win over Torino.

The 23-year-old looked particularly frustrated as he left the pitch in tears.

“He got injured, and I don’t know how long we’ll be without him,” Allegri remarked at a post-match press conference via TuttoNapoli.

“It’s very unfortunate; he was very down. I think the injury may be related to what he’s going through: this year he has different responsibilities, the national team, and greater mental pressure. Sometimes these injuries are caused by those things too.”.

Vergara, 23, has made ten appearances across all competitions this season with Napoli, scoring one goal and providing one assist.

However, he has already missed four club games due to a calf injury.

His latest injury is to the flexor of his left thigh, and according to Il Mattino, it’s unclear whether the versatile attacker will play for his club again in 2026.

During his post-match press conference, Allegri also spoke about the upcoming Champions League game against Manchester City, suggesting Napoli’s motivation might not be at its highest.

“It’s a very important match and a great one to play in,” Allegri said.

In a recent development, “We have to be realistic; our Champions League campaign will be decided against Club Brugge, Sabah and Viking. We had to beat Bodo, and we did. Tuesday will be very important and difficult, but we need to sort out the league, and the home match against Club Brugge will be crucial.”.

Anthropic IPO: four ways the AI giant wants to disrupt science
